Title: More firms miss Q3 earnings forecasts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More Malaysian companies are falling short of analysts' earnings expectations in the third quarter of financial year 2026 (Q3 FY26).
Consumer and property players bore the brunt of weaker sales, margin pressures and rising operating costs, CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said.
The firm said its beat-to-miss ratio had fallen to 0.58 times as at Nov 19, compared with 0.95 times in the preceding quarter and 0.78 times in the corresponding quarter last year, indicating a weaker earnings season.
Of the 52 companies under CIMB Securities' coverage that had reported results, only seven, or 13 per cent, exceeded expectations, while 12 companies (23 per cent) missed forecasts.
The remaining 33 companies, or 63 per cent, met expectations.
CIMB Securities said earnings disappointments were concentrated in the consumer sector, which accounted for four misses, followed by property and financial companies with two each.
Among the consumer companies that underperformed were Mr DIY Group Bhd, Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd, Amway (M) Holdings Bhd and Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd, with weaker sales, margin compression and higher operating expenses weighing on performance.
In the property sector, SP Setia Bhd and Eco World Development Group Bhd missed expectations due to slower conversion of domestic property sales, lower contributions from land sales and moderating construction profit margins.
However, aggregate earnings among companies under CIMB Securities' coverage grew 6.1 per cent year-on-year and four per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM8.22 billion.
The growth was supported by stronger contributions from technology, healthcare, transport and rubber glove companies.
Technology companies recorded the strongest year-on-year earnings growth of 104.6 per cent, followed by healthcare at 58 per cent and transport at 28.8 per cent.
The firm attributed the stronger performance among glove manufacturers to higher average selling prices, while Westports Holdings Bhd benefited from stronger cargo volumes.
Technology companies also recorded improved sales deliveries and margin expansion.
Seven companies exceeded expectations, including glove makers Hartalega Holdings Bhd, Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd and Top Glove Corp Bhd, alongside UEM Sunrise Bhd, ViTrox Corp Bhd, Westports and Nestle (M) Bhd.
Nestle Malaysia's performance was supported by improved margins and lower input costs, while UEM Sunrise benefited from higher contributions from joint ventures, mainly Horizon Hills and Nusajaya Tech Park.
Meanwhile, weaker earnings were recorded in plantations, non-bank financials and banking, which declined 10 per cent, 7.7 per cent and 5.1 per cent respectively.
CIMB Securities said the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI had retreated 6.8 per cent year-to-date to 1,566 points as at Nov 19.
This was weighed down by rising US bond yields, uncertainty surrounding US artificial intelligence (AI) chip export restrictions and weaker global technology sentiment.
"We will reassess our FBM KLCI target after the Q3 FY26 results season. Meanwhile, we advocate buying on dips, focusing on our preferred large-cap stocks, including 99 Speed Mart, SD Guthrie and Time dotcom," the firm said.
Following the latest results, CIMB Securities also upgraded 99 Speed Mart and RCE Capital Bhd to 'Buy' from 'Hold', and Genetec Technology Bhd to 'Buy' from 'Reduce'.
However, it downgraded Yinson Holdings Bhd to 'Hold' from 'Buy' and Aeon Credit Service (M) Bhd to 'Reduce' from 'Buy'.

Title: Cable thieves flee in Proton S70, Hilux after police chase
Article:
MELAKA: Police are hunting a group of cable thieves who escaped in two vehicles after a chase from Taman Malim Jaya to Rumbia early yesterday.
The 6.05am incident came to light after a 10-second video showing the thieves in action went viral.
Melaka Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said police rushed to the scene, where they found several people opening a manhole cover.
"Upon noticing our presence, they bolted in a dark blue Proton S70 and a white Toyota Hilux," he said in a statement.
This sparked a pursuit involving several police vehicles through Taman Malim Jaya, Batu Berendam, Krubong and Cheng before reaching Rumbia in Alor Gajah.
"However, both vehicles managed to escape. Efforts to track down the suspects are ongoing," he said.

Title: [UPDATED] Najib's house arrest: Pardons board minutes declassified to answer Bar's judicial review challenge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes regarding the granting of house arrest for Datuk Seri Najib Razak had to be declassified to answer a challenge by the Malaysian Bar.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said this was to enable the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) to file an affidavit to respond to the Bar's judicial review challenge over the issue.
"The document had to be declassified first to enable the attorney-general to prepare the affidavit. That's the position on the matter," he said.
Saifuddin said the A-GC's response would not be complete without details of what transpired during the Pardons Board meeting.
"As for who exposed it, what the purpose of exposing it was, I don't have (that information).
"The government is not in the position to explain on that," he told reporters at the PDRM Fun Run 2026.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had previously said the Pardons Board documents, classified as secret,
could be declassified
if they became subject to court proceedings.
He said the house arrest order for Najib was classified under the Official Secrets Act but would generally be declassified if challenged in court.
On Nov 11, the Malaysian Bar
filed an application
for leave to challenge the Pardons Board's proceedings and decisions relating to Najib's house arrest arrest, arguing that it was unconstitutional and had no basis in law.
The Bar also sought to temporarily suspend the house arrest arrangement pending the outcome of its judicial review application.
The A-GC said on Nov 12 it
would object
to the Bar's application, arguing that the matter was non-justiciable as it concerned the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's role in presiding over a Pardons Board meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kota Baru council clarifies bus stop upgrade plans after complaints
Article:
KOTA BARU: Almost 50 bus stops in Kota Baru are expected to be upgraded and repaired by next month, the Kota Baru Islamic City Municipal Council (MPKB-BRI) said.
In a Facebook post, the council said the project was funded by the Housing and Local Government Ministry, alongside its annual allocation.
The work is part of efforts to improve the city's appearance in collaboration with the National Landscape Department.
It said initial discussions had been held with MyBus and Konsortium E-Mutiara, with both giving positive feedback.
Site selection was based on safety, suitability and users' needs. The improvements would also cover bus stops not owned by the council.
The announcement followed complaints by volunteer group Hiyaz Community, which said a bus stop it had recently painted and cleaned ahead of the monsoon season had been demolished.
MPKB-BRI said it had contacted the group on Oct 26, before the project began, to explain the upgrading plans and invite discussions, but received no response.
The council regretted social media posts that it said had caused misunderstanding and negative perceptions. It welcomed public feedback and said information should be verified before being shared.

Title: [UPDATED] MCA vows to strengthen BN, secure more electoral victories
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  MCA is determined to secure more victories for Barisan Nasional, whether at parliamentary or state level, said its president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong.
He said MCA would remain a loyal and steadfast BN partner, pledging the party's continued support for the coalition's plans and initiatives.
"Whatever plans (BN chairman) Datuk Seri (Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi) may have, MCA, as a loyal partner in BN, will remain steadfastly by your side," he said in his address at the MCA Central Delegates general assembly.
Present were Zahid, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir; MCA deputy president Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon and party secretary-general Datuk Chong Sin Woon; MIC vice-president Datuk M. Asojan; and, People's Progressive Party deputy president Datuk K. Mohan.
Wee said consensus and unity remained the foundation of BN's strength.
"MCA will continue to serve as an agent of goodwill by fostering close and cordial ethnic relations and safeguarding harmony among Malaysia's diverse communities," he said.
He said, in the lead-up to the 16th General Election, MCA would continue working hard under the BN banner and pursue what was best for the party, whether the coalition contested independently, worked with strategic partners or through a consensus-based arrangement, as practised in Melaka.
"MCA's victories in the last three state elections showed that the party still has room to improve and win more seats, and that it will pursue this goal with humility.
"Datuk Seri (Zahid) himself reminded us after BN's victory in Melaka not to become complacent or boastful.
"MCA has taken that message to heart and will continue working hard on the ground. Certainly, this victory is not a licence for us to become complacent or let our guard down.
"That is why I have always reminded party members not to spend too much time celebrating electoral victories.
"Instead, we must remain focused on the people, continue helping communities and contribute to the development of the country," he said.
Wee added that MCA's experience in the Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka elections had seen the party double its number of seats won, from six to 12.
Meanwhile, he said MCA remains true to its identity and principles regardless of which political party or coalition with which it works.
Referring to a remark at the Umno general assembly recently, Wee said Zahid had stressed that regardless of whom Umno worked with, the party would remain Umno and BN would remain BN.
"I would like to add that MCA will always remain MCA," he said.
He said BN's fundamental values, including the spirit of consultation, inclusivity and respect for diversity, must remain the guiding principles of political cooperation, in accordance with the Federal Constitution.
He added that MCA was one of the founding parties of the Alliance, which later evolved into BN, adding that the coalition's power-sharing formula had been built collectively by its founding partners.
"MCA's principles remain unchanged, namely upholding the supremacy of the Federal Constitution, moderation, diversity and mutual respect among the races," he said.
On the electoral front, Wee said MCA would continue to uphold its core values regardless of the political cooperation model adopted.
"MCA's cooperation with any political party would always be guided by mutual respect, the Federal Constitution, the Rukun Negara and the rights and interests of all Malaysians."

Title: FBI probes suspected hack of criminal information database
Article:
NEW YORK: The FBI is investigating a suspected breach of a nationwide database used by federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday, citing two people briefed on the investigation.
The apparent compromise of the National Crime Information Centre database would mark the second intrusion involving an FBI system in recent months and the latest in a string of cyber incidents that have alarmed US officials over the past week.
The agency did not respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
The FBI database is used by law enforcement agencies nationwide to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks.
Previous high-profile cyber disruptions over the past week have included a global outage ​affecting hundreds of millions of Microsoft users and a nationwide halt to air ⁠travel that disrupted more than 18,000 flights.
A September breach by a digital extortion group ​known as "ShinyHunters" accessed an FBI jobs website, compromising data on current and former FBI employees.--REUTERS

Title: Paolo Bulgari, the Italian jeweller who turned a family business into global luxury brand, dies at 89
Article:
ATHENS, (Greece): Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who helped transform the family jewellery business into a global luxury brand synonymous with Italian glamour and design, has died. He was 89.
His family announced his death Saturday, describing him as "the greatest jeweller of our time" and praising his humanity and entrepreneurial talent, AP reported.
Bulgari presided for decades over a brand celebrated by supermodels, Hollywood stars and collectors for its bold designs and distinctive use of color.
Born in Rome in 1937, he was the grandson of Sotirios Voulgaris, who founded the jewellery business after leaving Greece.
Originally from Paramythia, a mountain village in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece renowned for its silver jewellery, Voulgaris fled Ottoman rule and settled in Naples before opening a shop in Rome, adapting both his craft and his family name to his new home.
Paolo Bulgari joined the family business shortly after leaving school.
Working alongside his father, Giorgio, he initially focused on precious stones, developing an expertise in gemstones that would inform his work as a designer and businessman throughout his career.
Turning away from the delicate aesthetic associated with Parisian jewellery houses, the Bulgari family embraced bold gemstones, rich yellow gold, generous proportions and unexpected combinations of color.
Drawing inspiration from ancient Rome and Italy's artistic heritage, the distinctive style helped set the brand apart internationally.
Alongside his brother Nicola and nephew Francesco Trapani, Bulgari led the company's expansion into major luxury markets, opening stores in New York, Paris, Geneva and Monte Carlo.
The business diversified beyond jewellery into watches, perfumes, leather goods and, eventually, hotels.
Heading the group since the mid-1980s, Bulgari guided the company through a period of significant international growth.
Its jewellery was a fixture on celebrities spanning from Elizabeth Taylor to Zendaya.
Tall and silver-haired, he occasionally appeared alongside the stars wearing his creations, maintaining a characteristically reserved presence.
In 2011, the family sold a controlling stake in the company to French luxury conglomerate LVMH in a deal valued at more than US$5 billion, ending decades of direct family control.
Despite his association with the glamorous world of international luxury, Bulgari frequently referred to his family's humble start.
In 2019, he and his wife established the Paolo Bulgari Foundation to support young people through schooling and job training in disadvantaged neighborhoods on the outskirts of Rome.
"Many people don't know it," he wrote in the foundation's introduction, "but at the origin of my surname there is a story of migration."
His funeral will be held Monday at the Basilica of Santa Croce in Rome. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Berjaya Property, Prince Court team up on healthcare perks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Property Bhd is partnering with Prince Court Medical Centre to extend healthcare privileges and medical-related services to buyers of selected residential developments.
These developments include Times Square 2 and The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Kuala Lumpur, the group said in a statement.
The collaboration will provide eligible homebuyers with access to healthcare privileges, medical assistance and wellness initiatives.
The two parties are also looking to organise health awareness programmes.
Berjaya Property group chief executive officer Syed Ali Shahul Hameed said healthcare access was an important consideration for property buyers, particularly foreigners looking to live in Malaysia for the long term.
He said the partnership was intended to complement the group's residential offerings by providing homebuyers with access to healthcare services in addition to location, connectivity and other facilities.
Berjaya Assets Bhd chief executive officer Tan Tee Ming said the collaboration was also aimed at attracting international buyers, amid continued interest in Malaysia as a destination for property investment and long-term residence under the Malaysia My Second Home programme.
He said the healthcare offering would add to the appeal of developments such as Times Square 2 and The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Kuala Lumpur, particularly among foreign buyers and families considering relocating to Malaysia.
Times Square 2, located along Jalan Imbi in Bukit Bintang, is about 3.4 kilometres from Prince Court Medical Centre.
The freehold development is connected to Imbi Monorail Station, Hang Tuah LRT Station, Berjaya Times Square and LaLaport Bukit Bintang City Centre via linked bridges.
The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Kuala Lumpur, along Jalan Sultan Ismail in the Golden Triangle, is about four kilometres from the medical centre.
The development offers residential services including concierge, valet parking and facilities such as a gymnasium, swimming pool and landscaped gardens.
Prince Court chief executive officer Tan Sok Kheng said the partnership would allow the medical centre to extend healthcare services to Berjaya Property homebuyers while promoting preventive healthcare.

Title: Malaysia respects ICJ judgment in Myanmar genocide case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia respects the International Court of Justice judgment delivered on Nov 19 in the genocide case brought by Gambia against Myanmar, the Foreign Ministry said.
"The ICJ's findings are in line with Malaysia's position on the protection of all vulnerable peoples," it said in a statement.
The ministry reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to upholding international law, including its responsibilities as a state party to the Genocide Convention.
It said Malaysia would also engage the United Nations, the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), Asean, and other stakeholders on matters arising from the judgment.
"Malaysia will continue to advocate for a comprehensive and durable resolution to the protracted crisis, including engaging all relevant parties to implement concrete measures to alleviate the plight of Rohingya sheltered in the country," it read.
The case was brought before the ICJ by Gambia in November 2019, alleging that Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention during its military crackdown against the Rohingya in Rakhine state in 2017 forcing hundreds of thousands to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh.
On Nov 19, the court ruled that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the convention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: 'This is our dignity': Onn Hafiz tears into management over Larkin Sentral upkeep [WATCH]
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi tore into Larkin Sentral's management over its rundown facilities, dirty toilets and years of poor maintenance during a surprise inspection yesterday.
"Do I have to teach you (to do something as basic as this)?," he told those responsible for maintaining the terminal, expressing frustration over the state of its facilities.
The 8.30am inspection followed mounting public complaints and criticism on social media, with Onn Hafiz confronting management over broken seats, dirty toilets, damaged escalators, faulty lifts and pothole-riddled roads.
He was particularly unhappy with the condition of the toilets, where there was even a small tree seen growing inside, despite users being charged 50 sen for access.
"Don't pretend to be doing the cleaning just because I am here," he said, questioning why maintenance was only being carried out when he turned up.
When a trader was asked to fully open his shutters, the response was that it had been faulty for years, prompting further questions over why the damage had remained unattended.
Passengers and patrons also urged Onn Hafiz to make regular visits, saying his presence could help expedite long-overdue repairs.
Some complained that upper-floor areas were unsuitable for business, while lifts frequently broke down and escalator works remained incomplete.
Taxi drivers also took the opportunity to raise complaints about the terminal's badly damaged road surfaces, riddled with potholes.
Onn Hafiz was also seen inspecting clogged drainage areas and questioning how long rubbish had been left there.
"If something needs repairing, then repair it. Can't you see the dirt? This is our maruah (dignity)," he said, referring to the terminal's condition and its importance as a gateway to Johor Baru.
He directed the Johor Public Transport Corporation (PAJ) and Larkin Sentral management to immediately repair damaged facilities, upgrade toilets, provide additional benches at passenger pick-up and drop-off areas and install more portable air coolers in waiting areas.
The management was also instructed to improve food court cleanliness, repair damaged road surfaces and review the bus ticket purchasing system, including additional charges imposed separately on passengers, to ensure greater transparency.
The latest inspection followed an open letter addressed to Onn Hafiz on Nov 11, highlighting dirty toilets, poor lighting, disorganised bus platforms and inadequate maintenance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 7 Sabah runners to compete in China trail championship
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Seven Sabah trail runners will compete in China from Nov 25 to 27, hoping to make their families proud and raise Mount Kinabalu's international profile.
Mount Kinabalu, at 4,095m, is Malaysia's highest mountain and one of Southeast Asia's best-known climbing destinations.
Sabah Youth, Sports Development and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan said their participation in the 2026 Asia-Pacific Trail Running Championship in Wuyishan would bring recognition to Sabah and Malaysia.
He said their experience in the Climbathon and trail-running competitions across Southeast Asia, as well as their familiarity with Mount Kinabalu's high-altitude terrain, would help them meet the challenges.
"Their success in China would be a source of pride for their families and the people of Sabah, while bringing international recognition to Malaysia.
"Their participation could also help promote Mount Kinabalu as an international trail-running destination," he said at a send-off ceremony at Kota Kinabalu International Airport.
Led by team manager Amylia Halil, the contingent will be spearheaded by Daved Simpat, who will compete in the men's 80km long trail alongside Milton Amat and Wilsen Singgin.
Osward Maikol, Sheron Sariman and Arikchely Ariyl Arikah will compete in the men's 40km short trail, while Lalitah Lintanga will represent Sabah in the women's category.
Nizam also praised the newly established Sabah Trail Running Association for preparing the team for the championship.
Daved, a 44-year-old Mount Kinabalu porter from Kampung Kiau, Kota Belud, said he hoped to inspire young people, particularly those from rural communities, to take up the sport and compete internationally.
With 13 years of ultra-trail running experience, he said the sport required patience, mental strength and consistent effort.
Daved finished third in the veteran category at last month's Climbathon. He will make his second appearance at the championship after finishing seventh at its inaugural edition in Uiju, South Korea, in 2024.
His work as a mountain porter also allows him to incorporate the physical demands of mountain activities into his training.
He hopes to finish among the top 10 in China.
"Do not give up if you fail. Keep working hard and do not be discouraged easily because this sport requires a long-term commitment," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pentagon moves to curb US-Canada military cooperation, report says
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has imposed new restrictions on military cooperation with Canada, according to US media, as the Pentagon said Saturday it was refocusing the relationship around American defence priorities.
Hegseth issued the directive in a classified memo circulated last week, The Washington Post reported Friday, citing officials familiar with the decision.
The precise scope of the restrictions was unclear, and the Post said it had not seen the memo.
"The Department of War is taking steps to ensure its engagements with Canada advance tangible US defence objectives and ultimately support a reinvigorated defence relationship," chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell told AFP, when asked to comment on the report.
He said Washington was "prioritising opportunities for bilateral cooperation" to strengthen the defence of the Americas, "while supporting Canada's ability to meet Nato obligations."
The Trump administration has devoted considerable military and diplomatic resources over the past year to fighting drug trafficking in Latin America, and has also consistently complained of Nato allies not spending enough on defence.
"This guidance does not impact defence intelligence cooperation, our binational NORAD command, or our cooperation through Nato," Parnell added.
NORAD is the joint US-Canadian command responsible for monitoring and defending North American airspace.
The reported restrictions come amid strained relations between the longtime allies under President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly suggested Canada should become the 51st US state.
Trump has imposed tariffs on Canadian goods and criticised Ottawa's defence spending, while Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has firmly rejected any suggestion of annexation.
Canada's Ministry of National Defence, when reached for comment on the Washington Post report, said in a statement that it "would not speculate on media reports of this nature."
"Canada and the United States have a long history of defence cooperation built on a shared commitment to continental defence and protecting our collective security around the globe. This collaborative work continues," said the statement, shared by spokesman Tony Wright.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IOI Properties CEO rebuts report: Earnings triple as it charts new course
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Properties Group Bhd has more than tripled its net profit and doubled its revenue since financial year 2019 (FY19) as it seeks to transform itself from a property developer into a group with two complementary earnings engines.
Group chief executive officer Datuk Lee Yeow Seng said its annual revenue increased from RM2.20 billion in FY19 to a record RM4.44 billion in FY26, while net profit expanded from RM661.3 million to RM2.15 billion over the same period.
He said the growth reflected the group's strategy of combining property development with a larger investment property portfolio to generate more stable recurring income across property cycles.
The group's share price also climbed from about RM1.20 in late 2019 to a high of RM4.62 in 2026.
Despite subsequent consolidation to around RM3, the share price remained 150 per cent higher than its 2019 level, Lee said.
He responded to concerns raised in a recent article by a financial portal on IOI Properties' debt profile, leadership transition and strategic direction.
"A recent article in The Edge has attempted to casting doubts on our debt profile, leadership transition, and strategic direction of IOI Properties Group Bhd.
"That it was published on the very eve of the Main Market debut of IOI Properties Group Malaysia Reit on Nov 25 warrants serious reflection.
"Given the sensitivity of this timing, as the group CEO it is my duty to address our shareholders and the investing public factually.
"The report is not an objective reflection of the group's position nor its potential."
Lee added that there is a deliberate and narrow focus on headline gearing ratios, while overlooking multi-year earnings expansion, healthy cash position and growth, embedded asset value, and clear capital-recycling roadmap.
"The report misses the broader financial reality of what we have built and where IOI Properties group's trajectory," he said in a statement.
Lee said focusing on headline gearing alone overlooked the group's earnings growth, cash position and underlying asset values.
He said the group had continued investing through challenging market conditions, including the Covid-19 pandemic, while tightening operational discipline.
Between FY22 and FY26, IOI Properties reduced its completed inventories by 62 per cent, from RM3.05 billion to RM1.17 billion.
At the same time, its investment property segment expanded significantly, with the portfolio exceeding RM37 billion across Malaysia, Singapore and China.
For FY26, the segment generated RM1.41 billion in revenue and RM851 million in operating profit, nearly four times the levels recorded in FY19.
Its hospitality and leisure business contributed another RM535 million in revenue.
Lee said recurring income was expected to contribute nearly half of the group's operating earnings once its Singapore assets reached a more stable operating phase.
The group's development business also continued to generate sales momentum, recording RM3.91 billion in property sales in FY26, with unbilled sales reaching a record RM2.51 billion.
Lee, who has led IOI Properties as group CEO since 2014, said the group's development over the years had been driven by expansion across residential, commercial, industrial and hospitality properties.
He said the strategy was to build an integrated property portfolio capable of generating both development profits and recurring rental income.
The group also doubled its dividend payout to 16 sen per share in FY26, from eight sen in the preceding financial year.
Lee said the Lee family, through Vertical Capacity Sdn Bhd and direct holdings, owned nearly 70 per cent of IOI Properties aligning its interests with the group's long-term performance and shareholder returns.

Title: One-off promotions from Jan 1 subject to merit, not automatic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Service Department (PSD) has set eligibility criteria for one-off promotions involving management and professional officers, effective Jan 1.
The promotions will not depend on vacancies or be automatic, but will be based on merit.
A letter dated Nov 17, signed by PSD director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz, states that eligible officers must be under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), confirmed in service and have served in their current grade for the required period by Dec 31, 2026.
Minimum service requirements vary according to the promotion grade:
— Grade 12 to Grade 13: At least six years in the current grade and 22 years of total service.
— Grade 10 to Grade 12: At least eight years in the current grade and 16 years of total service.
— Grade 9 to Grade 10: At least eight years in the current grade and eight years of total service.
Service in equivalent grades under the Malaysian Remuneration System (SSM) will also be taken into account.
Officers must also achieve a weighted performance score of at least 85 per cent over the past three years, with a minimum score of 85 per cent in the final year.
They must be endorsed by their department and service heads, have no disciplinary record as at Dec 31, 2026 and when their promotion is recommended to the board, and have declared their assets in accordance with regulations.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the one-off promotion under the Special for Incumbents scheme for 12,000 management and professional officers during the 2027 Budget presentation on Oct 9.
He said the move was to recognise high-performing officers who had been waiting for promotions because of limited positions.
Officers selected for the scheme must serve a one-year acting period before being promoted, subject to fulfilling the applicable promotion requirements and regulations.
Service heads are responsible for identifying eligible officers and submitting their names to the relevant promotion board secretariat under their respective human resources management divisions for consideration.
The recommendations must be submitted by June 30, next year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Time for a comprehensive National Student Suicide Prevention Strategy
Article:
LETTER:
A written parliamentary reply in March 2026 indicated that the Education Ministry's 2025 School Mental Health Screening Programme identified early signs of depression among 5.16 per cent of primary school pupils, while 5.48 per cent showed early signs of anxiety.
Importantly, the ministry indicated that mental health screening would be increased to twice yearly for all students from 2026, with more frequent screening for those identified in the severe and very severe categories.
The government has also strengthened cooperation between the Health and Education Ministries, including counselling, screening, early intervention and postvention services.
These are positive steps. However, implementation, accessibility and follow-up are crucial. Screening alone is not enough if students cannot obtain timely professional help.
Parents must learn to listen without immediately judging or criticising. Teachers must be trained to respond with empathy rather than punishment when students display emotional difficulties. Schools must become safe environments where students feel accepted and valued.
Friends and classmates should be encouraged to support one another and report concerns to responsible adults. NGOs, community organisations and mental health professionals should be encouraged to participate in prevention programmes.
We must remind our young people that seeking help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
Reports of student suicides should be handled sensitively.
The media should avoid sensational headlines, graphic details, descriptions of methods, speculation about motives, or assigning blame without evidence.
Instead, coverage should highlight:
•Suicide prevention and available support services.
•The importance of seeking professional help.
•Stories of recovery and resilience.
•The responsibility of schools, parents and society to protect young people.
The World Health Organisation has specifically issued guidelines on responsible reporting of suicide to minimise the risk of further harm.
I would like to propose that the government develop a comprehensive National Student Suicide Prevention Strategy involving the following five pillars:
1. Prevention by means of mental health education, anti-bullying programmes and a caring school environment.
2. Early Detection through regular mental health screening and trained teachers who can recognise warning signs.
3. Intervention through accessible counselling, professional assessment and timely treatment.
4. Family and Community Support through active parental involvement, NGO participation and community-based support networks.
5. Continuous Monitoring and Postvention through follow-up care, support for affected students and prevention of further tragedies.
These recommendations are consistent with WHO guidance on school-based suicide prevention, which emphasises social and emotional skills, staff training, parental involvement and access to external support services.
We cannot afford to lose another young life because we have failed to recognise a child's emotional distress or failed to provide the support that he or she desperately needs.
Academic excellence must never come at the expense of mental well-being. Our schools must not only produce academically successful students but also emotionally healthy, confident and resilient young people.
We must stop treating mental health as a secondary concern. The mental and emotional wellbeing of our children must be regarded as equally important as their physical safety and academic development. Every child matters.
Every life matters. No student should feel that suicide is the only way out of his or her problems.
If a student expresses suicidal intentions or appears to be in immediate danger, the school and family must take it seriously, ensure the student is not left alone, obtain urgent professional assessment, and contact emergency services where necessary.
In Malaysia, HEAL 15555 provides mental health crisis support, while 999 should be contacted in an emergency.
All NGOs should consider making student mental health and suicide prevention part of their wider community safety agenda. Protecting children is not confined to protecting them from physical dangers. It must also include protecting their emotional and psychological wellbeing.
A school should be a place where children feel safe, respected, supported and hopeful about their future. That is the kind of educational environment we must strive to build.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Member

Title: EU proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
Article:
BRUSSELS: The EU put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget Saturday, as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding.
European Council President Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros (US$224 billion) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous.
"I believe this proposal can bring us closer to a final agreement," Costa told a press conference in Brussels.
EU countries have been squabbling over the size of the next budget, with Germany leading calls for major cuts after the commission last year proposed a two-trillion-euro budget for the 2028-2034 period.
Berlin criticised a revised proposal published last month that suggested slashing the bloc's future seven-year budget by 140 billion euros.
Costa, who represents the EU's 27 states, is seeking to reach a deal by the end of the year balancing contributions from member states with new sources of revenue for the bloc.
Among these could be a tax on digital firms, which the draft Costa presented Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than 750 million euros.
They would be subjected to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3 per cent of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data", according to documents shared by the council.
The plan is likely to provoke US President Donald Trump's ire since his administration has reacted angrily to EU fines and moves against Big Tech under its content and competition rules in recent years.
"This tax is in no way directed against any particular company or country," Costa said of the levy, which replaces a charge on large companies envisaged by the commission.
The draft also includes plans for a levy on electronic waste and higher tobacco taxes. Costa said the EU will explore a tax on crypto assets and to gain revenue from radio spectrum auctions.
Overall the council estimates the EU's "own resources" could generate about 60 billion euros in revenue each year.
PARLIMENT THREAT
The draft will be at the centre of hours of fraught talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.
Costa is pushing for a deal in December, amid EU fears that a delay would push talks into a fraught election year in 2027 with worries about what potential eurosceptic victories in France and elsewhere would mean for future dealmaking.
Once EU states find an agreement, they will have to negotiate with parliament -- a task that also promises to be difficult.
"President Costa's proposal is simply unacceptable. The Council is fixated on cuts when Europe needs ambition and resources to tackle its mounting challenges," key budget lawmaker Siegfried Muresan warned.
Germany and five other so-called "frugal" EU members, including Sweden, are pushing in the opposite direction.
"We are still a long way from a compromise. The budget is still too large," Swedish Europe Minister Jessica Rosencrantz wrote on X after the latest draft was unveiled.
Costa does not only have to contend with the frugals' demands.
France, the second-biggest EU economy and a net contributor to the budget, argues the bloc needs sufficient means to match the rising challenges it faces.
Meanwhile, 17 countries from southern, central and eastern Europe have formed a group known as the "Friends of Cohesion" and are pushing for greater funding to support agriculture and regional development.

Title: Executive loses RM617,159 to friend in fake loan, investment scam
Article:
KULAI: A 29-year-old executive lost RM617,159 when a man he had known for eight years allegedly duped him through bogus loan requests and a non-existent car accessories investment promising 45 per cent returns.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said the victim had transferred money to the suspect 72 times into six bank accounts between Nov 30, 2022 and March 12 this year.
The suspect first approached the victim in 2022 for a loan before offering him shares in a car accessories business on Dec 22, 2024, promising a 45 per cent return within a year.
The victim, who trusted the man, agreed to both arrangements and made the transfers online but failed to recover either the loans or investment capital.
His attempts to contact the suspect failed when he discovered that his telephone number had been blocked.
He lodged a police report yesterday.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a jail term of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.

Title: Fossil fuel dispute threatens to scupper climate deal
Article:
TURKIYE: Global climate talks dragged into a second day of overtime Sunday as a standoff over fossil fuels threatened to derail a final deal at the UN COP31 summit in Turkey.
Nations braced for another long night of negotiations after a draft climate deal stripped all mentions of coal, oil and gas, sparking threats of a walkout.
The COP31 presidency convened hasty meetings between opposing camps in a bid to bridge the gulf and produce an acceptable text more than 24 hours past the scheduled close.
The European Union and Saudi Arabia -- deeply divided over the future of fossil fuels -- were brought together to seek a compromise.
At a plenary in the wee hours of Sunday, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum told delegates that a third and "final" text would be sent to them for review.
Kurum said negotiators would have until 6:00 am (0400 GMT) "to come to us with agreement on the text" and that a closing plenary would then be convened.
"We ask you to look at this decision carefully," Kurum said. "We are closer than ever to agreement on the remaining issues."
European Union climate envoy Wopke Hoekstra had warned on Saturday: "It's better to have no deal than to have a bad deal."
Expectations of a major breakthrough in the Turkish city of Antalya have been low as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.
The summit follows a string of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia and unfolds as a super El Nino pattern amplifies the risk of further extreme weather.
A draft climate deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas.
RED LINES
Fossil fuels are the main driver of climate change but a flashpoint at the UN talks. Their omission from the draft sparked protests and threats to walk away from the table.
"That is a red line for us. We're talking about the root cause of all of this," Tuvalu's Climate Minister Maina Talia told reporters.
Talia, whose low-lying Pacific nation is threatened by rising sea levels, said if the world cannot address fossil fuels "then we are wasting our time here".
Ireland's Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien said there were around "130 countries at this COP who want -- at the very least -- a reference to fossil fuel and phase-out" in the final text.
A call to ramp up carbon capture -- a contentious technology championed by the fossil fuel industry -- in the last draft also faced staunch opposition.
Critics point to its high cost and meagre record in cutting emissions, warning it risks prolonging fossil fuel use.
"There are several fights but the primary one is still the one between mostly the EU and Saudi Arabia" over fossil fuels and carbon capture, said Li Shuo, an analyst from the Asia Society Policy Institute.
Panama's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, has also threatened to scuttle any weak deal, accusing a "petroleum mafia" of holding the world hostage.
CLEAR ELECTRIFICATION
Facing pressure over fossil fuels, COP31 hosts Turkey and Australia have pitched "electrification" as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security.
The latest draft "cover decision" proposed a target to electrify the global economy -- a push to replace technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, like diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives.
The proposal calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035.
But it does not require that the additional electricity come from renewable energy rather than coal or gas, spurring some countries to demand an explicitly "clean" target.
Around one-third of global electricity is produced using coal and another fifth using fossil gas.
Attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya to delay the next set of reports by the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) have been another major source of friction.
Countries have also disagreed over how to respond to the looming breach of the 1.5C warming target set under the Paris climate accord.
The latest draft expressed "deep concern" over missing the goal but dropped an earlier call to return warming below 1.5C as soon as possible this century.
The talks are also jammed over long-running complaints that rich nations are shirking their obligations to help developing nations confront climate change.
The removal of a US$120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

Title: Mexico captures FBI most-wanted drug kingpin as 11 killed in raid
Article:
MEXICO CITY: Mexico's military announced Saturday that it had captured a drug kingpin on the FBI's list of 10 most wanted fugitives in an operation that left four soldiers and seven suspected gunmen dead.
Fausto Isidro Meza, alias "Chapo Isidro," was captured Friday night during a special forces raid in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, along with his alleged second-in-command and a financial operator for his criminal organisation.
The Mexican defence ministry said seven suspected attackers were killed and eight people arrested during the operation, including the three senior gang figures.
Four soldiers sent to reinforce security in the town of Guasave were also killed as gang members mounted fierce resistance to their leader's arrest, it said.
The military seized a .50-caliber rifle, a grenade launcher, grenades, other firearms, drugs and cash. It said there were no reports of civilian casualties.
The operation sparked panic across the surrounding area, with gunfire forcing the suspension of a professional baseball game in Guasave, local media reported.
Unverified videos posted on social media showed people running inside the stadium amid shouts of "Get down, get down!" as bursts of gunfire rang out nearby.
Another video appeared to show a hovering military helicopter firing a machine gun.
Violence also erupted in other parts of Sinaloa, where suspected gang members erected improvised roadblocks.
An unverified video circulating on social media overnight appeared to show a detained Chapo Isidro urging his associates to stand down, warning that "children, women, innocent people" could be put in harm's way.
The violence echoed the aftermath of a military operation in February that killed Nemesio Oseguera, alias "El Mencho," leader of the powerful Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG).
His supporters retaliated by setting fire to businesses and blocking roads across 20 of Mexico's 32 states.
- US INTELLIGENCE 'COORDINATION' -
Chapo Isidro, 44, is the leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions of the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico's military said.
He faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States.
The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives, while the US State Department offered a reward of up to US$5 million for information leading to his arrest.
Giving his name as Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, the FBI bulletin said his group is responsible for importing "large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States."
In July, Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a longtime leader of the Sinaloa cartel, was sentenced to life in prison in New York.
Zambada was a former associate of notorious drug trafficker Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman, who was extradited to the United States in 2017 and is also serving a life sentence.
Chapo Isidro's capture comes just days after Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum met US counterpart Donald Trump on the sidelines of a summit in Asia.
Trump, who has pushed Mexico to do more to tackle drug gangs, said Friday that the two had discussed trade and security.
"We're working with her on the cartels because the cartels are running Mexico. I told her that, and we can't let the cartels run Mexico. They're our neighbour," he told reporters at the White House.
The Mexican military said the operation was conducted "following coordination" with US intelligence in the "framework of bilateral cooperation."
Earlier this year, Sheinbaum faced political pressure over revelations that US intelligence personnel were operating in Mexico without her government's approval following the deaths of two reportedly CIA agents in a road accident.--AFP

Title: Central Hat Yai mall to serve as flood evacuation point for tourists
Article:
HAT YAI: Central Hat Yai shopping mall will serve as a gathering point for tourists, including Malaysians, stranded by floods.
Malaysian Consul-General in Songkhla Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi said the mall would serve as a gathering point for affected tourists before they were evacuated.
The initiative was jointly organised by the Songkhla Tourism Industry Council, Hat Yai Hotel Association and the shopping mall.
"This is a precautionary measure in preparation for possible floods, similar to those that hit the city last year.
"Malaysian tourists stranded by floods need not worry. They can contact rescue teams, who will gather them at Central Hat Yai before arranging their evacuation," he said.
Fahmi said local authorities had taken various measures to assist those affected and ensure tourists' safety, including setting up safe zones.
More than 6,000 Malaysian tourists were stranded during major floods in the city in late November last year, requiring evacuation and assistance.
He said Malaysians travelling to Thailand, particularly during the current monsoon season, should monitor weather updates and forecasts and take comprehensive travel insurance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drug smuggling by RMAF personnel: Police were on the case since January
Article:
KULIM: Police began monitoring Royal Malaysian Air Force personnel for suspected drug smuggling in January.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said continuous intelligence-gathering efforts had convinced federal police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department in July that drug smuggling activities involving RMAF assets were taking place.
He said the air force personnel had been using RMAF assets to transport drugs from one location to another as the security controls were not as tight as other the country's other entry and exit points.
"Following the recent arrest of our (commercial airlines) co-pilot in Jakarta, the Home and Transport ministries stepped up and tightened security measures at the country's entry and exit points, particularly at Kuala Lumpur International Airport.
"This undoubtedly affected smuggling syndicates, forcing them to turn to alternative methods of smuggling, including through ports and other channels.
"They then resorted to using RMAF facilities to transport drugs from one point to another, and the 96kg of drugs detected (smuggled in using RMAF assets) is a substantial amount," he said.
Saifuddin said this to reporters after a Moral Values Programme in Kampung Paya Besar, Lunas, near here last night.
Saifuddin said cooperation between NCID and RMAF eventually paid off, with the authorities confirming trafficking activities involving the transportation of drugs from Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah when checking luggage.
This, he said, confirmed the involvement of civilians and RMAF personnel.
"The RMAF personnel involved are still being held in remand, and police are focusing on determining whether this was indeed the work of a syndicate, how long the operation had been running, and whether it took place only on the day of the arrests or had been going on earlier.
"We do not yet know whether the syndicate is local or foreign, as those arrested include both civilians and military personnel. However, given that more than one person is involved, there is a possibility that a syndicate is operating behind the activities, and we do not rule out further arrests," he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had, while in Shenzhen, revealed that several RMAF personnel, including pilots, were involved in drug smuggling.
NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan later said five air force personnel were
among 11 people
arrested, with 96.64kg of drugs worth RM4.83 million seized.
On Saturday,
two more
RMAF personnel were arrested.

Title: Housewife loses RM111,631 in online investment scam
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A housewife lost RM111,631 after falling for a fake online stock investment scheme promising quick returns.
Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the woman came across an investment advertisement on Facebook on Oct 14 and contacted the number listed.
She then dealt with two people who explained the investment terms and promised high returns within a short period.
"Convinced by the offer, she followed their instructions and transferred money in stages to six different bank accounts," he said in a statement today.
Azli said all dealings were conducted online, with no face-to-face meetings between the victim and the individuals involved.
The woman used her own savings to invest.
"She realised she had been cheated after making 16 transactions totalling RM111,631 without receiving any returns.
"She lodged a police report about 11.30am yesterday," he said.

Title: Drug smuggling: Entry, exit point security controls may be extended to RMAF bases
Article:
KULIM: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants to extend security controls at the country's entry and exit points to include the areas surrounding military and police air bases.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the prime minister will bring the matter to the cabinet for discussion this coming week.
This follows the arrests of several Royal Malaysian Air Force personnel for drug smuggling recently.
Saifuddin said Anwar was concerned because numerous air bases across the country, which are under military control, as well as those operated by the police through its Air Operations Force, are vulnerable to smuggling activities.
"When this incident (the arrests of the RMAF personnel) occurred, I was with the prime minister in Shenzhen, where he briefed me on the security controls at the country's entry points under my ministry, through the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA), among other agencies.
"So, (Anwar) has a proposal which he will bring to a cabinet meeting specifically convened to discuss this issue," he told reporters after attending the Moral Values Programme in Kampung Paya Besar, Lunas, near here, last night.
Saifuddin said the ministry's main focus at present was to ensure that prohibited substances are not brought into or taken out of the country through its official air entry points.
He said, however, that there was a possibility of extending the role to other air entry points following the incident involving RMAF personnel.
"Are our security controls limited to official entry points, excluding security force bases such as those operated by the military and police? For instance, the police have bases for the Air Operations Force, while the RMAF also has numerous air bases of its own.
"Our current focus is on controlling entry points, but following this incident, the prime minister has raised the question of whether the Home Ministry should review the matter," he said.
Anwar, while in Shenzhen, had revealed that several RMAF personnel, including pilots, had been arrested for drug smuggling.
On Thursday, federal police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said five RMAF personnel were among
11 people arrested
in the Klang Valley and Labuan.
They were detained on suspicion of being involved in the smuggling and distribution of 96.64kg of drugs worth RM4.83 million using RMAF assets.
Yesterday, two more RMAF personnel were
arrested
in Tawau.

Title: Frederica Fabian Peter crowned Mrs Global World Malaysia 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Borneo model and mother Frederica Fabian Peter was crowned Mrs Global World Malaysia 2026.
The pageant's grand final was held on Friday. Dedicated exclusively to married women, it celebrates confidence, individuality and women's achievements, particularly those of mothers.
Dr Meneka Menon was named first runner-up, while Jesslyn Tan, N. Evelyn Sharmini and Dr S. Saraswathy took the second, third and fourth runner-up positions respectively.
National director Sharon Jasmin congratulated the winners and praised all 10 contestants for their efforts throughout the competition.
"It must have been difficult for the judges to choose a winner as everyone performed exceptionally well.
[[nid:1583060]]
"These are 10 beautiful mothers who stand strong, embrace their individuality and inspire others through confidence and courage," she said.
Jasmin, a former pageant queen, said winning a title required more than preparation, highlighting the importance of initiative, sound judgement and forward thinking.
"Above all, it is about reading between the lines, understanding what is expected and putting what has been learned into practice," she said.
She hoped the winners would continue to inspire others, contribute to their communities and uplift women through their voices, leadership and actions.
The five-member judging panel included Mayasilk Group fashion director Deepa Khiyani, Talent Innovation chief executive Carl Graham and Mrs Universe 2013 Carol Lee.
Lee, who has competed on the international pageant stage, brought her experience to the panel, emphasising beauty beyond physical appearance and the importance of inner elegance.

Title: Australia criticises US Congressional Budget Office over AUKUS comments
Article:
SYDNEY: Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles on Sunday criticised the United States Congressional Budget Office over a report that said the AUKUS pact would decrease the number of attack submarines available to the US Navy.
"They are wrong," Marles said, referring to the CBO, which said in the report this month that the sale of Virginia-class submarines to Australia could diminish the size of the navy's attack submarine force through to 2060.
AUKUS, Australia's largest-ever defence project, will put US-commanded Virginia-class submarines in Australia from next year, involves selling several Virginia-class submarines to Australia from around 2030 and will have Britain and Australia build a new class of AUKUS nuclear-powered submarine.
Marles was not worried about the report "because AUKUS is very much happening" and "the production rate in the United States is absolutely increasing", he said in televised remarks.
In October, Marles said Australia remained on track ​to acquire its first ​nuclear-powered subs from the US in the early 2030s.
The CBO did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours.
Canberra has committed A$368 billion (RM999 billion) over three decades to AUKUS, including billions of dollars in investment in British and US production bases.
Formed in 2021, AUKUS is part of efforts to counter China's growing influence in the Indo-Pacific. China has called the pact dangerous and warned it could spur a regional arms race. — REUTERS

Title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's Likud for Israeli coalition talks
Article:
JERUSALEM: Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday.
Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday, reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government."
Former military chief Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.
Saturday's announcement comes as Eisenkot's wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu's bloc.
"In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow," the party said in a statement.
Former prime minister Naftali Bennett, an important figure in Eisenkot's camp, on Saturday called for a "Zionist unity government headed by Eisenkot" and said his party would refuse to join up with Netanyahu or his bloc.
Netanyahu has been pushing hard for a national unity government, which he says is needed to guarantee Israel's security.
Shortly after Eisenkot's announcement, Likud laid out its position on forming such a government with Eisenkot's bloc, including demands to halt "all personal attacks and incitement" as well as political "boycotts" against Netanyahu and the government.
Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu's Likud, but has previously ruled out serving in a government led by Netanyahu himself.
Likud also called for a joint declaration committing to a unity government including "all parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people" and without the participation of Arab parties.
Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly criticised leaders of Arab parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a "terror group" following its Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel. All leaders of Arab parties have condemned the attack.
Likud proposed a set of guidelines for a unity government including an agreement that Israel is the nation-state of the Jewish people, a rejection of Palestinian statehood, the maintenance of Israel's "security zones" in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza, and an arrangement on the issue of ultra-Orthodox conscription into the military through a "broad agreement" with the community's leaders.
On Friday, Eisenkot vowed not to let coalition-building talks drag on and said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail.--AFP

Title: 8,180 flood relief centres ready to accommodate 1.86 million people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  A total of 8,180 temporary flood relief centres (PPS)  nationwide have been prepared to accommodate up to 1.86 million flood victims during the northeast monsoon.
The Social Welfare Department said RM77.8 million has been allocated to strengthen its flood preparedness, with funds channelled towards improving disaster management, purchasing essential supplies and upgrading storage facilities.
To ensure an uninterrupted supply of food and other necessities, particularly in high-risk areas, the department has coordinated 824 storage facilities and 835 small- and large-scale suppliers nationwide.
The logistics network includes 550 forward bases in interior areas at risk of being cut off by floods, supported by eight Disaster Relief Storage Depots, eight state stores, 144 district stores and mini container depots.
The department said registration of flood victims at relief centres had been streamlined through QR code scanning via the InfoBencana system.
"The public can also use the latest digital ecosystem through the MyIBJKM 4.0 application to pre-register and check the locations of the nearest PPS," it said.
Meanwhile, human resource preparedness has been strengthened with the deployment of more than 4,800 department officers, some 800 Psychological Support Team members and 2,200 volunteers.
To protect staff welfare and prevent fatigue among personnel on the ground, the department has implemented a shift  system, with rotations every 24 to 48 hours.
It had also conducted 40 PPS management training and simulation sessions involving around 6,000 participants to ensure smooth flood operations throughout the monsoon season.

Title: Fire and Rescue Department deploys 25,592 personnel for monsoon season
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Fire and Rescue Department has placed 25,592 officers and personnel on standby, backed by 1,248 operational assets, for the northeast monsoon, which is expected to last until March.
Its director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad, said preparations included strengthening land, marine and air capabilities to ensure swift search-and-rescue operations and flood evacuations.
The department has identified 3,682 flood hotspots nationwide based on Drainage and Irrigation Department data.
Nor Hisham said its main  assets included 571 light transport vehicles, such as four-wheel- drive and utility vehicles, and 144 heavy vehicles, including lorries.
"These vehicles are suitable for navigating flooded roads and delivering supplies to victims.
"Emergency Medical Rescue Services  ambulances have also been strengthened to provide initial medical assistance at disaster sites.
"In addition, the department has 529 marine assets, including rescue boats of various sizes, supported by its elite Water Rescue Team," he said.
[[nid:1582944]]
s
The department has also supplied 150 boats to communities in high-risk areas to facilitate early evacuations while awaiting  rescue teams.
For aerial surveillance and aid delivery to areas cut off by floodwaters, the department has four helicopters and three drones to carry out real-time monitoring.
It has also activated Regional Forward Bases  in three key locations — Penang for the northern region, Terengganu for the east coast and Johor for the southern region — to reduce response times and streamline assistance to affected areas.
These bases are supported by 29 Rapid Deployment Teams, which are ready to be mobilised at any time, Nor Hisham added.
Before the monsoon season,  fire stations nationwide had conducted a flood operations testing and inspection day to gauge their readiness, ensuring that boat engines, heavy machinery and rescue equipment were in optimal working condition.
The inspections also involved 62 engineering personnel.
On manpower management, Nor Hisham said leave restrictions  have been imposed according to operational needs, particularly in high-risk states such as Selangor and on the  east coast.
In Kelantan, the state Fire and Rescue Department is looking at extending work shifts to 24 or 48 hours in the event of major floods to ensure sufficient personnel  on the ground.
Coordination with other rescue agencies through the Disaster Operations Control Centres and local community leaders has also been stepped up to identify vulnerable residents, including senior citizens, people with disabilities and bedridden patients, before water levels rise.
The department has urged the public not to underestimate the risks posed by extreme weather during the monsoon season.
The public are advised to temporarily suspend water-based recreational activities, including swimming, picnicking and camping near rivers, rapids, waterfalls and irrigation canals, due to the risk of sudden water surges.
Hiking in monsoon-affected areas, as well as swimming in the sea should also  be temporarily avoided to avoid the risks of slippery trails, landslides, lightning strikes and strong waves.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Civil Defence Force  has mobilised 12,927 personnel and strengthened its rescue assets nationwide.
Its deputy chief commissioner (Operations), Ghazali Abd Rahman, said more than 7,000 full-time personnel were ready for deployment and would be supported by volunteers in the event of massive disasters.
Separately, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, in a statement in the Dewan Rakyat on Thursday,  said the government was prepared to mobilise more than 100,000 security and technical personnel, with nearly 2,500 boats under the National Disaster Management Agency's (Nadma) coordination.
Nadma, he added, was also preparing 1,100 lorries, 28 aircraft and 35,000 life jackets.

Title: Collaboration with Bersatu no cure to PH's Malay dilemma
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan's best bet to shore up Malay support ahead of the next general election may be limited cooperation with Bersatu, although even that is unlikely to deliver significant gains, analysts say.
"Many voters have made up their mind to not vote for PH even if PH manages the economy well or lowers living costs," said Sunway University political scientist Professor Wong Chin Huat.
Wong said although the swing voters whom PH hopes to win over had shrunk, the coalition still needed to manage the economy and cost of living well as the leading coalition in government.
He said the recent Melaka election offered PH its best possible strategy, where it and Bersatu avoided contesting against each other in certain seats.
The move was aimed at preventing vote splitting against Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional candidates, but proved ineffective in stopping the "Blue Wave", which swept all Malay-majority seats in last week's Melaka polls.
Wong said a full alliance with Bersatu would be counterproductive for PH, as their past conflicts could risk further alienating the coalition's support base.
"The best way is the Malacca model, no contest in some constituencies and contest in some others."
However, Wong said even this "best way" might not significantly help either PH or Bersatu.
"The high transferability of votes between BN and PN means many seats would become uncompetitive," he said.
Wong said low non-Malay voter turnout, if repeated in the next general election, could also hurt PH.
"The Chinese turnout in Malacca was estimated to be 20 percentage points lower than the Malays. While this wasn't enough to hurt PH in Malacca, it might lose many seats in GE16."
At the same time, Wong said DAP, the party with the most seats in PH, would remain a convenient target for the coalition's rivals.
He said many DAP leaders needed to improve their "Malay cultural literacy", citing the backlash against Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong's comments on the enforcement of shop closures during Friday prayers in Terengganu.
However, he said this did not change the fact that DAP remained an easy target.
[[nid:1583082]]
"Even DAP leaders who are close to Malays and understand Malay cultures well like Steven Sim and Howard Lee were not spared from attacks."
Nusantara Academy of Strategic Research senior fellow Professor Dr Azmi Hassan also said a PH-Bersatu tie-up would do little to improve their electoral fortunes.
"Bersatu just cannot deliver on the Malay votes which PH really needs.
"The three state polls show that Malay voters have no qualms voting either for a BN or PN candidate."
Azmi said DAP and the actions of some of its leaders had also helped fuel cooperation between BN and PN.
"So I don't think an alliance between PH-Bersatu will make a difference, especially as Melaka has demonstrated. Bersatu cannot steal the votes from BN-PN.
"In fact, Bersama did much better in terms of stealing votes compared to Bersatu."
Azmi said PH should instead try to exploit issues that could strain cooperation between BN and PN, particularly over seat allocations.
"This will be the main issue between BN-PN. PH should look at offering BN better seat allocations. Between BN and PH, there will be a minimum overlap."

Title: EU, Indonesia sign 'ambitious' trade deal, paving way for 2027 rollout
Article:
BRUSSELS: The EU and Indonesia officially signed a trade deal to open up their markets in Brussels on Saturday, paving the way for the accord to come into force early next year.
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen and Indonesian Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto attended a signing ceremony for a pact that Brussels said is projected to increase European Union exports to Southeast Asia's largest economy by almost 40 per cent within 15 years.
"This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," said von der Leyen, the European Commission president.
EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic and Indonesia's minister for trade Budi Santoso were also in attendance.
"Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," von der Leyen added, thanking Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, who she said will visit Brussels on Dec 11.
Negotiations for the deal were concluded last year, almost a decade after they were launched, as part of a wider EU push to diversify trade as it faces challenges from the United States and China.
The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the ancillary Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) will open investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals, Brussels said.
The pact removes tariffs on more than 98 percent of European exports to the world's fourth most populous country including food, agricultural and industrial products and will help save over 600 million euro (US$658 million) a year in customs duties, according to the EU.
Around 90 per cent of Indonesian exports to the EU will be tariff-free, Airlangga said, noting that is expected to benefit the country's top shipments to the bloc including palm oil, footwear and textiles fisheries.
"The benefits for our exporters are concrete and measurable," he said, hailing a "new chapter" in economic relations with the EU.
Palm oil and deforestation had posed stumbling blocks to the negotiations, and the pact includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues as well as a dedicated protocol on palm oil to allay some of the related concerns.
Brussels said the deal will boost economic growth, with the EU's GDP projected to be 16 billion euros higher and Indonesia's 27 billion euros higher by 2042 than they would be without the agreement.
The European Parliament has to greenlight the pact and Indonesian authorities complete the ratification process before it can provisionally come into effect.--AFP
