Title: No shortcuts, no instant paste: How Banglo289 keeps traditional Malay cuisine authentic at mid-market prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 —  In an increasingly competitive food and beverage industry, the use of instant ingredients and commercial pastes has become a common choice among food operators, particularly to save preparation time and reduce costs.
However, Banglo289, a restaurant serving traditional Malay cuisine from various states, has chosen to go against the grain by using fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods to preserve the authenticity of its dishes.
The restaurant also offers a unique dining concept, combining an upscale and comfortable setting with prices aimed at the mid-market segment.
“The idea behind setting up this restaurant actually stemmed from our observation of a gap in the market for traditional food, particularly Malay cuisine, served in a comfortable setting at reasonable prices.
“Usually, if customers want to enjoy this type of food at affordable prices, roadside stalls are their best option, but the surroundings may not be very comfortable. If they prefer a more comfortable setting, there are exclusive restaurants, but they have to pay premium prices,” its Chief Executive Officer Shareen Farzida Sukri told Bernama.
Making heritage cuisine accessible
Banglo289 seeks to bridge that gap by offering an exclusive dining environment and a wide selection of dishes, allowing customers to choose their preferred food and portions according to their tastes and budgets.
The Kelantan-born entrepreneur from Kuala Krai said the average spending of between RM30 and RM50 per person per visit recorded by the restaurant did not refer to the fixed price of any particular dish, but rather the total amount customers typically spent during each visit.
“This includes a combination of rice, side dishes, vegetables, porridge, desserts, fruits and traditional cakes, all reflected in a single bill,” she explained.
The menu also varies according to dining hours, with different selections available for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Recounting the restaurant’s establishment in 2022, Shareen Farzida said that, as its name suggests, the premises occupy a century-old bungalow located along Jalan Raja Chulan here.
Within four years of operation, the restaurant brand has expanded to four outlets at different locations across the Klang Valley, with plans to open more branches in other states nationwide.
Balancing costs and business sustainability
The expansion has also brought greater responsibilities, particularly in ensuring that the concept and quality of food remain consistent across all outlets, a task Shareen Farzida acknowledged posed challenges, especially in terms of costs.
Using fresh ingredients, including spices, requires employees to prepare basic ingredients themselves, such as fresh chillies, onions and turmeric.
“The cost of fresh coconut milk alone reaches RM50,000 a month for all our outlets. We adopt this approach to ensure the authenticity of our food.
“Previous generations, such as our mothers and grandmothers, rarely or never used instant ingredients, possibly because of preservatives and chemicals that could affect the original taste of the dishes,” she said.
To demonstrate its commitment to preparing basic ingredients from scratch without relying on instant pastes, the restaurant has incorporated open-kitchen concepts near the serving counters at almost all its outlets, allowing customers to observe the cooking process firsthand.
Minimising food wastage
Shareen Farzida said rising raw material prices were managed through careful operational planning to ensure that the restaurant did not compromise on food quality.
“Among the cost-saving measures we have introduced are those that do not affect the taste of our food, such as opting for simpler decorations and food presentation that are not overly elaborate but remain neat and visually appealing.
“We also focus on improving workforce management by arranging staff shifts and allocating duties according to peak and off-peak hours, ensuring productivity remains high without placing an excessive burden on salary costs,” she explained.
The restaurant also prioritises efficient raw material management, with each outlet having its own purchasing team to source fresh ingredients according to the respective kitchen’s requirements.
“Raw ingredients must be used on the same day and cannot be kept for use on another day.
“We have adopted this approach to minimise wastage and keep our overhead costs under control. This is why dishes are prepared in stages and in small batches of only about 10 to 15 servings at a time, with no leftover dishes kept for the following day.
“If a particular dish is in high demand, additional portions can be prepared as long as operating hours and the availability of raw ingredients permit,” she said.
She added that the restaurant sometimes had to explain its concept to customers, particularly its practice of preparing food in controlled quantities to maintain quality and prevent wastage.
Nevertheless, she said certain best-selling dishes, such as smoked beef cooked in coconut milk with bird’s eye chillies (daging salai masak lemak cili api), were always made available to customers.
Traditional cooking
To preserve the authenticity of its traditional dishes, Banglo289 also takes the initiative to learn heritage cooking techniques directly from their original sources.
Banglo289 Business Development Director Datuk Mohd Hafidz Safari Ramli said research teams, usually comprising between six and 12 chefs, travelled to selected states, including Kelantan, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Johor, to meet veteran cooks and local communities who still possessed knowledge of traditional food preparation.
“This research is an ongoing learning process. Each visit is not merely about obtaining a list of ingredients, but also understanding the entire process, from selecting raw materials and determining measurements to the sequence of cooking steps and the time required to produce an authentic dish,” he said.
He added that the teams would revisit the original sources if their attempts to recreate a dish did not meet the desired characteristics, whether in terms of taste, colour or texture.
Every recipe and cooking method learnt is documented as a reference for the chefs, helping to ensure consistent food quality even when dishes are prepared by different individuals.
Citing Kelantan’s nasi dagang as an example, he said the team not only learnt its preparation methods directly from local sources in the state but also sourced ingredients, including spices, from there.
For patin fish cooked in fermented durian paste gravy (patin masak tempoyak), the research team travelled to Temerloh, Pahang, to understand the balance of sourness and the distinctive consistency of the gravy.
Meanwhile, the preparation of smoked beef in coconut milk with bird’s eye chillies involves manually smoking the meat over rambutan wood and coconut shells for approximately eight hours.
“All these are part of the preparation process that cannot simply be bypassed. If we want to preserve our cultural heritage through food, we must do it properly and uphold the true meaning of the word ‘heritage’,” he said.
Reviving endangered heritage dishes
Apart from preserving the authenticity of traditional dishes that remain familiar to the public, Banglo289 is also committed to reviving heritage cuisine that is becoming increasingly difficult to find, particularly dishes that are no longer widely prepared by restaurant operators or younger generations.
Shareen Farzida said the initiative, known as ‘Endangered Recipes’, stemmed from her team’s observations of the diversity of traditional food in several locations, including dishes that were known or still prepared by only a handful of food operators and elderly cooks.
Among the dishes identified for preservation are lemang periuk kera, kulat sisir masak lemak, lawar terung and bubur anak lebah, each with its own distinctive ingredients and preparation techniques.
Citing bubur anak lebah as an example, she explained that the traditional sweet delicacy, made from a rice flour-based batter, requires considerable manual skill and a special mould to shape tiny pieces resembling baby bees before they are cooked until chewy and served with sweet coconut milk gravy.
Preparing such unique dishes requires patience and direct guidance, as the techniques cannot necessarily be mastered through written recipes alone, she said.
She added that the team’s visits to several states had also uncovered dishes that were prepared only during Ramadan or certain festive seasons, limiting opportunities for younger generations to discover and learn how to make them.
This has raised concerns that the knowledge and skills involved could disappear if those who still possess them pass away before having the opportunity to pass them on.
“That is why we plan to collaborate with Yayasan Hasanah, an impact-driven foundation under Khazanah Nasional Berhad that actively supports the preservation of local arts, heritage and culture, to fund the production of a special documentary on this ongoing project.
“Heritage cuisine is not merely a cultural treasure to be printed on a menu. It is a body of knowledge and a cultural identity that must continue to be cooked, savoured, documented and passed down properly, without shortcuts,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Thailand only a transit route for drug syndicates targeting Malaysia, says Kelantan police chief after 700kg meth bust
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 21 — Malaysia-Thailand cross-border security cooperation has continued to strengthen, with authorities in the neighbouring country successfully preventing more than 700 kilogrammes of methamphetamine from entering Malaysia.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the success demonstrated the Thai authorities’ commitment to combating drug smuggling activities that use the country as a transit route before the drugs are brought into Malaysia.
He said Thailand was not the main destination for the drug smuggling activities but served primarily as a transit route for syndicates involved in cross-border crime.
Mohd Yusoff said Kelantan police had previously held meetings with the Thai authorities to strengthen security cooperation, particularly in combating drug smuggling and criminal activities along the border of the two countries.
“The Thai authorities have taken steps to tighten security by setting up checkpoints to prevent cross-border criminal activities, including the entry of drugs into Malaysia.
“What we have implemented on our side has also been adopted by Thailand, and they have now stepped up their security measures. We are grateful for the cooperation and commitment shown,” he told reporters after an engagement programme with young bikers at the Kelantan police contingent headquarters here today.
Mohd Yusoff said close cooperation between the two countries was important to ensure that border routes were not exploited by syndicates to carry out drug smuggling activities.
He said enhanced joint security measures could also help curb the movement of syndicates using cross-border routes to smuggle illicit substances into the country. — Bernama

Title: Four teenagers under 15 arrested after ramming police car during chase on North-South Expressway
Article:
IPOH, Nov 21 — Police detained four underage teenagers (under 15 years old) for allegedly obstructing public servants from performing their duties at Kilometre 286.5 of the North-South Expressway heading north, near Simpang Pulai, yesterday.
Tapah district deputy police chief DSP Mohd Fadzil Ismail said a team of officers on patrol duty received information at 4.20 pm yesterday from the Tapah district police headquarters (IPD) control centre to assist officers from the Ringlet police station in tracking down a Toyota Cherry multi-purpose vehicle occupied by several individuals suspected of being involved in a kidnapping case.
He said that following the information, police officers moved to the Batu 3 area, Jalan Pahang, near Tapah, to conduct a surveillance and the vehicle involved was successfully detected at about 5.30 pm.
“The police instructed the driver of the vehicle to stop for inspection, but the driver failed to comply with the order and instead sped off, nearly hitting the on-duty police officer.
“The police officers then gave chase to the vehicle all the way to the Tapah toll plaza area. In an effort to intercept the suspect’s vehicle, the police vehicle’s bumper was hit by the suspect’s vehicle,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Fadzil said another police vehicle from the Ipoh district police headquarters joined in the chase before the suspect’s vehicle was successfully intercepted at Simpang Pulai.
He said all four suspects were arrested, and the vehicle they used was seized.
According to him, the initial investigation found that all those detained were teenagers and the results of the urine screening tests showed that they were all drug-free and had no previous records.
“The three teenage boys who were detained have been remanded for four days starting today, while a teenage girl was granted police bail as she is involved in an ongoing investigation in Jitra, Kedah,” he also said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code as well as Section 279 and Section 353 of the same code. — Bernama

Title: Don’t push your child into a boarding school if they’re not ready, Fadhlina tells parents as Education Ministry weighs more wardens and counsellors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The Ministry of Education is looking into the need to increase the number of assistant wardens and guidance and counselling teachers to ensure students receive optimal attention and support while staying in hostels.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the aspiration of parents to see their children gain admission to fully residential schools should be balanced with the children’s own abilities and emotional readiness.
“As we plan for our children’s future, it is important that we also listen to their voices and understand their feelings. Our dreams as parents must align with our children’s own abilities and emotional readiness,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, she said that she had held discussions with the police in Kuala Kangsar, Perak, on strengthening the safety and well-being of students residing in the hostel of the educational institution concerned.
The discussions covered compliance with standard operating procedures, hostel management, and the importance of parents assessing their children’s level of readiness before sending them to boarding schools.
Fadhlina said every child had a different level of adaptability, with some adjusting quickly while others required more time, adding that some children were able to cope well with academic competition, while others needed greater encouragement.
As such, she stressed the importance of creating an environment where children could share their thoughts and be heard without being judged.
“I want parents to know that we share the same hopes. We want our children to succeed, but more importantly, we want them to grow up safe and happy,” she added.
She also advised parents not to be overly concerned if their children do not gain admission to their dream schools, as every child has his or her own unique path and timeline for achieving success.
“Most importantly, regardless of where they study, they must know that our love and acceptance never depend on the name of their school or their examination results,” she added. — Bernama

Title: Bumiputera firms are listing on Bursa, but Akmal Nasrullah wants them to go bigger
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Five Bumiputera companies successfully listed on Bursa Malaysia between April 2025 and September 2026, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
The companies are Orkim Bhd, which was listed on the Main Market, and SumiSaujana Group Bhd, Elsa Bhd, GTA Holdings Bhd and United Asiapac Energy Bhd, which were listed on the ACE Market.
Akmal Nasrullah said the listings demonstrated the potential of Bumiputera enterprises to grow, attract investment and gain access to broader capital markets.
“Our next challenge is to build on this progress by enabling more Bumiputera enterprises to scale up, compete in higher-value industries and become market leaders,” he said in his opening remarks at the YP Leadership Conference 2026 here today.
He highlighted that under the 13th Malaysia Plan, Malaysia aims to raise its economic potential while raising the floor of living standards.
“The Bumiputera Economic Transformation Plan 2035 complements this direction by advancing meaningful Bumiputera participation, ownership and competitiveness.
“Human capital development is fundamental to both agendas, but it must be closely linked to enterprise growth and economic opportunities,” he said.
“This is where the complementary roles of Yayasan Peneraju, the Bumiputera Agenda Steering Unit (Teraju) and Ekuiti Nasional Bhd (Ekuinas) become especially important.
“Together, their mandates support an ecosystem that develops talent, strengthens enterprises, facilitates business expansion and promotes long-term economic ownership,” he added.
He said Yayasan Peneraju identifies and nurtures high-potential talents to become value creators in professional, business and community spheres.
Meanwhile, Teraju supports the development and expansion of Bumiputera enterprises, while Ekuinas contributes through investment, business transformation and long-term value creation. — Bernama

Title: Pahang puts RM450,000 into hunt for invasive redtail catfish threatening native fish
Article:
TEMERLOH, Nov 21 — The Pahang government has allocated RM450,000 for a programme to control the redtail catfish population, which has been identified as a potential threat to the state’s native fish population if left unchecked.
Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the programme, being carried out simultaneously at seven locations statewide, including Pekan and Jerantut as well as Temerloh, was aimed at reducing the population of the invasive fish species.
He said the redtail catfish was a predatory alien species that could threaten the survival of other native fish species sharing the same habitat.
“The state government takes the issue of redtail catfish very seriously as this is an alien species that can threaten existing fish populations.
“If left unchecked, it could wipe out native species because it is highly aggressive and preys on other fish, eventually becoming the dominant species,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating at the Pahang 1st: Tawan Baung Ekor Merah Fest programme at Dataran Pekan Sehari, Kuala Krau, here today.
Wan Rosdy said one of the programme’s activities was a redtail catfish fishing competition to encourage members of the public to catch as many of the fish as possible.
He expressed hope that the initiative would help reduce the population of the species and protect native fish from the threat of extinction.
Meanwhile, Wan Rosdy said the Pahang government would provide assistance to federal civil servants in the state in the form of goods or non-cash contributions under the state budget tabled yesterday.
He said the approach was adopted in view of the state government’s financial constraints in providing cash assistance to the large number of federal civil servants. — Bernama

Title: National health fund, cheaper insurance by 2027: Economy Ministry’s healthcare reform wish list
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The Ministry of Economy has outlined four strategic priorities to support the healthcare reform agenda under the 13th Malaysia Plan, focusing on healthcare investment, financing sustainability, industry and talent development.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the priorities would complement the Health Ministry’s role through national development planning, resource prioritisation and cross-sectoral coordination.
He said the first priority was aligning healthcare investments with population needs, taking into account access to services, avoidable delays, workforce availability and operational resources.
The second priority was to strengthen healthcare financing sustainability by exploring the establishment of a national health fund and a strategic purchasing platform, as well as enhancing public-private collaboration in selected services, including diagnostic imaging, elective surgery and virtual specialist consultations.
“The Reset Strategy addresses pressures on private healthcare costs, including through price transparency and insurance reform. A key initiative is the base medical and health insurance and takaful plan, with market introduction targeted for early 2027.
“These efforts should complement the public healthcare system. Cost containment should never come at the expense of clinically appropriate treatment,” he said when officiating the 35th Malaysian Urological Conference (MUC) 2026 here today.
Also present were MUC chairman Dr Arvind Vashdev Jagwani, newly elected Malaysian Urological Association (MUA) president Dr Toh Charng Chee, and KPJ Selangor consultant urologist Prof Datuk Dr Khairul Asri Mohd Ghani.
Akmal Nasrullah said the third priority was to develop healthcare as a high-value economic sector, particularly in medical devices, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, digital health and clinical research, with efforts focused on moving beyond importing and using technology towards developing and commercialising more Malaysian solutions.
He said the fourth priority was to strengthen healthcare talent and professional capabilities, including training capacity, staff retention, geographical distribution and the mix of specialist skills.
Meanwhile, Akmal Nasrullah said prostate cancer cases recorded in the Malaysia National Cancer Registry Report 2017-2021 increased to 6,441 from 4,189 in the 2012-2016 period, with 63.3 per cent of cases for which staging information was available diagnosed at Stage III or IV.
He encouraged the MUA to contribute to evidence-informed policymaking by sharing data on waiting times, treatment outcomes and patient-reported quality of life. — Bernama

Title: Two vehicles, one viral cable heist: KL police on the hunt for daring thieves outside TREC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The police are actively tracking down a group of individuals suspected of stealing cables in front of the TREC premises on Jalan Tun Razak here, after the incident was recorded and went viral on social media today.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said his team received a report regarding a 38-second video uploaded on the Threads platform at around 9.50 am today.
He said the incident that occurred during the day involved a group of individuals using two vehicles while cutting cables at the location.
“During the incident, all the suspects fled after being approached by the public. Efforts to track down all the suspects involved are currently underway,” he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Section 235 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and Section 379 of the Penal Code.
Fadil also advised the public who have information about the incident to contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2115 9999, the Wangsa Maju District Police Headquarters Hotline at 03-9289 9222, or any nearby police station.
Earlier, a video went viral on social media showing several individuals believed to be stealing cables in an area near a road using two vehicles, including a four-wheel drive. — Bernama

Title: Sejingkat Bridge won’t shut Pending Port, Sarawak deputy premier tells DAP critics
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 21 — Caretaker Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas has hit out at the Democratic Action Party (DAP) over its criticism of the Sejingkat Bridge, dismissing claims that the project would force Pending Port to close and cause job losses as malicious allegations.
He said the criticism failed to take into account the Sarawak government’s wider plans for port infrastructure, recalling how opposition figures had gone to the opposite riverbank to record videos criticising the project.
“They sarcastically claimed that the Sarawak government had made a mistake in constructing this bridge because Pending Port would close and people would lose their jobs.
“That is why these people never appreciate what we have done,” he said when delivering his welcoming speech at the official opening of the Sejingkat Bridge here on Friday night.
Rejecting the claims, Uggah maintained that Pending Port would remain operational, pointing out that the bridge’s 26-metre clearance would allow most cargo vessels to continue passing beneath it.
He said the critics had also failed to recognise that caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg had wider plans for Sarawak’s port infrastructure, including the construction of a new port.
Uggah further pointed out that facilities for roll-on/roll-off vessels at Senari Port had been completed, with capacity to accommodate up to 3,000 vehicles at a time.
“The GPS government has plans, unlike DAP, which only knows how to blame others. These are malicious allegations,” he said.
The impact of the Sejingkat Bridge on Pending Port had previously been raised by Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen, who questioned restrictions on vessel access and whether Senari Port had sufficient capacity to accommodate additional cargo traffic.
The Kuching Port Authority had earlier maintained that Pending Terminal remained operational despite concerns over the bridge’s impact on shipping activities.
Turning to the state’s infrastructure development record, Uggah said the Sarawak government had demonstrated its ability to deliver major projects despite earlier scepticism over its bridge-building programme.
He said 21 of the 22 major bridges under the programme were being implemented by the Public Works Department Sarawak at a combined cost of RM6.55 billion, while another bridge was located in Lawas.
All the projects, he stressed, were funded using Sarawak’s own financial resources.
Recalling criticism when the programme was first announced, Uggah said the completion of major crossings had transformed road connectivity and reduced reliance on ferry services, particularly along the Kuching–Miri route.
“Today, travelling by road from Kuching to Miri no longer requires taking ferries. Ferries are now a thing of the past. They belong in museums.
“This is a gift from GPS and the Premier to the people of Sarawak,” he said.
Uggah also credited Abang Johari’s leadership with strengthening Sarawak’s financial position, enabling the government to undertake major infrastructure projects and introduce initiatives such as free tertiary education.
He said Sarawak’s revenue had increased from RM5.9 billion in 2016, with the state targeting RM15.01 billion next year.
Citing these development achievements, Uggah urged Sarawakians to remain united and continue supporting Gabungan Parti Sarawak and Abang Johari’s leadership in the coming state election, saying the state’s development agenda remained unfinished. — The Borneo Post

Title: ‘Sarawakians are smart’: Abang Johari welcomes BN, PAS decision to skip Sarawak polls
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 21 — Caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg has welcomed announcements by several non-local political parties that they will not contest in the 13th Sarawak Election, saying Sarawakians are capable of managing their own affairs without outside interference.
The Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman said Sarawakians were well capable of looking after their own state and that outsiders should not interfere in its affairs.
He noted that commercial banks such as Hock Hua Bank and Bank Utama have ceased to exist but Sarawak has gained ownership of Affin Bank.
He also mentioned that Sarawak had acquired Bintulu Port for RM1.8 billion and set up a state-owned oil company, Petroleum Sarawak Berhad.
“Sarawakians are smart, we are smart. Outsiders should stay out of the way. Some parties have publicly stated that they will not be contesting (in the next state election), and we appreciate this.
“But if anyone wants to challenge us, we will fight for Sarawak’s harmony,” he said at the Serian Sarawakku Sayang 2026 Programme held at the Serian Convention Centre on Saturday.
Abang Johari, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) president, said he was not campaigning for GPS as nomination day was only a few days away.
However, he added: “We look after Sarawak. We develop Sarawak and Sarawak will continue to progress and prosper.”
He then called out, “Sarawak”, to which the crowd responded, “First”.
Earlier this week, Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced that the coalition would not contest any seats in the upcoming Sarawak election.
“BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in the state,” he said when met by reporters at a Deepavali open house in Kuala Lumpur.
Also earlier this week, Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan announced that the party had decided not to contest in the 13th Sarawak Election.
In a response, PAS Sarawak commissioner Mohammad Arifiriazul Paijo said the state chapter accepted the decision, taking into account the prevailing political dynamics.
The Election Commission has set December 12 as polling day for the 13th Sarawak Election, with nomination day and early voting taking place on November 28 and December 8, respectively. — The Borneo Post

Title: Fadillah: Sarawak should maximise its rights through negotiation, not by undermining Federation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof has reminded Sarawak that its pursuit of state rights must not come at the expense of the Federation, but should instead strike a balance between the interests of both sides.
He said the best approach was to maximise the rights that Sarawak was entitled to through negotiations and cooperation with the Federal Government.
“We cannot pursue our demands to the point of undermining the interests of the Federation because we are a federation. This means we have to balance the interests of both sides,” he said during a dialogue session at the 2026 ‘Abas Orang Kamek’ (AOK) programme for the Klang Valley zone at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) here today.
He was responding to a participant’s question on Sarawak’s direction and its efforts to reclaim the state’s rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
Fadillah said cooperation between the state and Federal governments was necessary as certain matters fell under their respective jurisdictions.
For example, he said Sarawak’s plans to sell energy to Singapore and Peninsular Malaysia, involving routes through Indonesian waters, required approval from Indonesia through the Federal Government.
Fadillah also said efforts were underway to ensure that Yayasan Sarawak or the state government had its own building in Kuala Lumpur to provide accommodation for students and Sarawakians coming to the city for medical treatment.
Meanwhile, he said AOK had replaced ‘Lan Berambeh Anak Sarawak’ in Kuala Lumpur this year due to a packed schedule of events in Sarawak in November and December.
Fadillah, who is also patron of Sarawak Volunteers, hoped Lan Berambeh could be held again in the coming years.
The AOK programme, organised by Sarawak Volunteers, brings together Sarawakians living, working and studying in Peninsular Malaysia to exchange views and obtain updates on developments in the state. — Bernama

Title: Ismail Lasim’s palace pledge vindicates us, Negeri Sembilan Pakatan says, urging BN and Perikatan to retract claims
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 21 — Negeri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan (PHNS) has described Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s stance on defending the royal institution and complying with decisions concerning the state’s customs and Constitution as being in line with the principles upheld by the coalition since the crisis erupted in the state.
The state PH Leadership Council said the stance should provide an opportunity for the public to reassess various allegations levelled against the coalition during the recent Negeri Sembilan State Election campaign, including claims that it had interfered in customary affairs, influenced the palace and threatened the position of Islam.
“Hence, the state PH demands that the leaderships of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) retract those baseless allegations.
“If BN and PN have evidence to support the allegations they previously made, they should present it openly. Otherwise, the allegations should be withdrawn and corrected,” the state PH said in a statement today.
Yesterday, Ismail was reported to have pledged allegiance to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, and vowed to uphold the royal institution’s sovereignty, abide by the State Constitution 1959 and comply with decisions of the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.
Meanwhile, PHNS said allegations that the Negeri Sembilan palace was controlled by DAP, that the coalition’s leaders had interfered in customary affairs and that the position of Islam had been threatened under the previous administration were baseless.
PHNS also reaffirmed its commitment to continue playing the role of a responsible opposition, defending the sovereignty of the royal institution, respecting customs and the Constitution, and advocating policies and administration that prioritise the people’s welfare. — Bernama

Title: UKM logo to ride on Pocket Rocketman Azizulhasni’s jersey all the way to LA 2028
Article:
BANGI, Nov 21 — The Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) logo will now feature on the jersey of national track cycling champion Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang at international competitions, potentially including the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games.
UKM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh said the strategic partnership would see Azizulhasni appointed as UKM Global Ambassador, with the university also planning to become the main sponsor of the cyclist, popularly known as The Pocket Rocketman, until the Olympic Games.
He said Azizulhasni was chosen not only for his sporting achievements but also for his international influence and reputation, which could help introduce UKM to the global community.
“We want to bring UKM’s good name to the global stage. Therefore, we need a prominent figure who is internationally recognised to carry the university’s logo and name. From now on, the UKM logo will be seen on Azizulhasni’s jersey.
“We will be his main sponsor at every competition leading up to the 2028 Olympics so that people around the world will get to know UKM,” he told reporters after the 54th UKM convocation ceremony, which was officiated by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, here today.
Azizulhasni was conferred an Honorary Doctor of Philosophy (Sports Development) degree at the ceremony.
Sufian said the partnership was also in line with UKM’s aspirations to expand its international influence through academic networks and strategic collaborations, including the university’s presence in Qatar and efforts to strengthen ties with Timor-Leste and Kenya.
He said Azizulhasni was also expected to engage with the campus community through interactive sessions and experience-sharing programmes to inspire students.
Meanwhile, Azizulhasni described his appointment as UKM Global Ambassador as a major responsibility to bring the university’s name to the international stage through his participation in major competitions.
“Every time I compete overseas, especially at major competitions such as the Olympics, we will carry UKM’s name onto the international stage, insya-Allah. After more than 20 years as an athlete, I feel this honorary degree is one of the highest forms of recognition I have ever received. It is not only a source of motivation but also a great responsibility,” he said.
Azizulhasni said he hoped the recognition would open the eyes of more young athletes to the importance of pursuing sporting excellence and academic achievements in tandem, while proving that success in sports was no obstacle to furthering one’s education.
“We should not focus solely on sports but must strike a balance between sports and education. Learning is not limited by age; it is something we must pursue throughout our lives.
“As for me, insya-Allah, after retiring from sports, I would like to continue my studies, preferably at UKM,” he said.
Earlier, in his speech after receiving the honorary degree, Azizulhasni shared his story of overcoming a health crisis that had nearly ended his sporting career following heart surgery in 2022.
He said a sports cardiologist in Melbourne had once advised him not to place too much hope in returning to compete at the highest level due to his health condition at the time.
“I could either accept those words as the end of my journey or keep trying and persevering. At that time, I chose to continue the fight,” he said.
The Tokyo Olympic silver medallist said he had been diagnosed with a congenital coronary artery abnormality known as Anomalous Right Coronary Artery, a rare condition affecting less than one per cent of the world’s population.
He said his determination to return to the world stage eventually paid off when he won four gold medals at international competitions this year — two at the UCI Track World Cup in Perth and Nilai, as well as one each at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games and the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. — Bernama

Title: Promised quick gold returns, Terengganu retiree pays out RM131,820 before smelling a rat
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Nov 21 — A retiree lost RM131,820 after falling victim to an online investment scam.
Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 59-year-old woman joined a gold investment scheme advertised on Facebook on October 30.
He said the victim, who communicated with a male suspect via WhatsApp, invested her retirement savings after being promised lucrative returns within a short period.
“The victim made 38 payments totalling RM131,820 into four different bank accounts between October 30 and November 19.
“However, to obtain the promised returns, she was asked to pay another RM19,000, purportedly for processing fees,” he said in a statement today.
Azli said the victim, who became suspicious and realised she had been cheated, lodged a police report at 12.25 pm yesterday.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: ACP stands for Assistant Commissioner of Police.

Title: Paralympian, hockey forward and sprinters among Perak honours for Sultan’s 70th birthday
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Nov 21 — Perak Public Works Department (JKR) director Zamri Mat Kasim topped the list of 208 recipients of state honours and medals conferred by Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah today in conjunction with the Ruler’s 70th birthday at Istana Iskandariah here.
Zamri was the sole recipient of the Darjah Dato’ Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk.
His Royal Highness was accompanied by Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim.
Also in attendance were Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah.
Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and his wife Datin Seri Aezer Zubin.
Today’s recipients were part of the 218 individuals who were conferred state honours and medals in conjunction with the Sultan’s birthday, which was celebrated on November 6.
Universiti Teknologi Petronas deputy vice-chancellor Prof Dr Abd Rashid Abd Aziz, National Registration Department (Management) deputy director-general Raja Azlal Raja Azman and Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris deputy vice-chancellor Prof Dr Raja Nor Safinas Raja Harun were among 11 recipients of the Darjah Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini.
Sultan Nazrin also conferred the Darjah Paduka Mahkota Perak (PMP) on 31 recipients, including Perak and Kedah Orang Asli Development Department director Hairulnizam Abd Rahman and Perak Fire and Rescue Department deputy director Yusri Mohd Yusoff @ Hashim.
Other PMP recipients included the chief secretary to the government’s special officer, Dr Wan Mohd Hasif Wan Muhamat Ali, and Ayer Kuning assemblyman Dr Mohamad Yusri Bakir.
Bernama Perak Bureau chief Syamsiah Sahat was among 19 recipients of the Darjah Ahli Cura Si Manja Kini.
In addition, 48 individuals received the Darjah Ahli Mahkota Perak, while 52 others were awarded the Pingat Pekerti Terpilih.
Paralympic cyclist Nur Suraiya Muhamad Zamri and national hockey forward Muhammad Azrai Aizad Abu Kamal were among 34 recipients of the Pingat Jasa Kebaktian, alongside national sprinter Muhammad Azeem Mohd Fahmi and national women’s sprinter Shereen Samson Vallabouy.
A total of 12 individuals also received the Pingat Lama Perkhidmatan. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JKR stands for Jabatan Kerja Raya in Malay while PMP stands for Paduka Mahkota Perak.

Title: Penang CM Chow Kon Yeow promises answers on Perak water deal as Lim Guan Eng keeps up the heat
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 21 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today said he will hold a press conference in the next few days to explain the state’s RM24.6 billion water supply deal with Perak, after repeated criticism from DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng.
“I will arrange a press conference in the coming days. In the meantime, he can keep on providing his views,” Chow told reporters here, as quoted by news portal Free Malaysia Today.
Lim, the former chief minister and Air Putih assemblyman, has repeatedly raised the matter on social media.
Lim has been critical of the arrangement under which the Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) would pay Perak RM210 million a year for 40 years, even if no treated water is supplied.
He accused Chow and state executive councillor Zairil Khir Johari of failing to explain the rationale for that condition.
In his latest remarks yesterday, Lim accused Chow of acting unethically and of failing to respect professional judgement and sound financial considerations.
Chow has said the 40-year agreement includes safeguards against supply shortfalls and allows PBAPP to terminate it in certain circumstances.
Chow also accused Lim of misleading the public despite repeated explanations.
Asked if it was appropriate for leaders from the same political camp to criticise each other publicly on social media, Chow declined to comment directly.
“That is for the person who made those remarks to answer,” he was quoted as saying today by The Star.

Title: Penang Umno-Pakatan pact must hold till end of term, says Chow Kon Yeow as PKR rep sounds alarm
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 21 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today said the Pakatan Harapan (PH)-Umno partnership was meant to last until the end of the current term and should not be reopened every time someone grumbles.
He was reacting to PKR’s Fahmi Zainol, the Pantai Jerejak assemblyman, who had questioned why DAP still keeps an Umno representative in the Penang government, several local news outlets reported.
“But his own party is working with Umno at the federal level, isn’t it?” Chow was quoted by Free Malaysia Today as telling reporters after attending the opening ceremony of the 37th International Baba Nyonya Convention here.
Chow, who is also Penang PH chairman, said state leaders could voice their views but the final say on cooperation with Umno rested with the PH central leadership.
“We cannot be holding meetings every week to discuss this matter,” the DAP central executive committee member was quoted as saying by The Star.
The Star also quoted him as saying the federal agreement came with a commitment to complete the term and “should be respected as long as the agreement itself is honoured”.
Chow dismissed Fahmi’s criticism as a personal opinion.
Asked whether Penang DAP would review its ties with Umno, Chow said that was a matter for the national leadership, The Star reported.
Fahmi, a former Penang state executive councillor, raised the issue in a TikTok video posted on Wednesday.
He asked how long DAP would keep Umno in the state government and warned that PH could regret it and lose the next state election.
According to Free Malaysia Today, Fahmi noted the barbed exchanges between DAP and Umno in the run-up to the Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka state elections.
Umno’s sole representative in Chow’s administration is Sungai Acheh assemblyman Rashidi Zinol, who holds the rural development, agrotechnology and food security, and entrepreneurship portfolio on the state executive council.
The Penang PH is scheduled to meet on November 28 to discuss its working relationship with Umno in the state.
Chinese vernacular newspaper Guang Ming Daily reported that Penang PKR met on November 17 and, citing party insiders, said it discussed reviewing the appointment of Umno leaders as local councillors, state constituency coordinators and village community management council members.

Title: Azmin at Amanah convention: Delegates clap, Pakatan-Bersatu watchers take note
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 21 — Dressed in blue, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali walked into the Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) National Convention here this morning, and the hall took notice, Sinar Harian reported.
The Malay-language daily said he arrived at Dewan Raja Muda Musa in Section 7 and was seen chatting warmly with Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and deputy president Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa.
Delegates greeted him with applause and cheers the moment his name was announced by Amanah secretary-general and National Convention 2026 director Muhammad Faiz Fadzil.
His presence stood out, Sinar Harian noted, because of the shifting ties between Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu.
PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun was also present.
Mohamad Sabu delivered his presidential address before officiating the two-day convention.
Azmin was once firmly on the other side of that divide, as PKR deputy president, former Selangor menteri besar and economic affairs minister in the PH government after the 2018 general election.
That ended on February 24, 2020, when PKR sacked him and Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin, and nine other PKR MPs followed them out, in what became known as the Sheraton Move.
The move, together with Bersatu’s exit from PH, brought down the coalition government after 22 months and put Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin as prime minister.
Azmin joined Bersatu about six months later, served as international trade and industry minister under Muhyiddin, and was named Bersatu secretary-general on November 28, 2024.
PKR said in June 2022 that it would not work with him, and he lost the Gombak parliamentary seat to Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari at the general election that year.
He bounced back in the August 2023 state election, winning the Hulu Kelang state seat by 1,617 votes over PH’s Juwairiya Zulkifli.
In August this year, he said he would never return to PKR, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the party president and PH chairman, replied that he was not aware of any invitation to Azmin.
Bersatu had also denied in May that it planned to return to PH, but on November 11 Azmin said the party had not ruled out a last-minute understanding with PH in the Melaka election campaign.
Azmin was seen stumping for Amanah during the recently concluded Melaka election.

Title: Perak water or bust: PBAPP says Penang has run out of options after 98pc EGM vote
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 21 — Penang’s RM24.6 billion plan to buy treated water from Perak has won the backing of 98 per cent of shareholders in PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB), the parent company of the state water utility, at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) here today.
Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) chief executive officer Datuk K. Pathmanathan said the state’s Water Contingency Plan 2030 had run out of options within Penang, The Star reported.
“There is nothing left, so the only available opportunity is the Perak water source,” he was quoted as saying after the EGM.
He said PBAPP had compared the project with seawater desalination, which would cost substantially more and lead to a higher tariff.
“That is why we consider this project the best practical alternative for PBA,” he added.
Pathmanathan added that the minimum purchase of 300 million litres per day (MLD) was conservative, given the demand from Penang’s growing industrial sector and incoming investments.
“So we need more and more water,” he was quoted as saying, pointing to companies signing agreements and launching investments in Batu Kawan even as the EGM was under way.
Also present were PBAHB group chairman and Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, State Secretary Datuk Jafri Abdul Jalil and PBAHB chief financial officer Mary Ann Harris.
The 40-year deal runs from 2032 to 2072 and covers a minimum of 300 MLD of treated water from a new 500 MLD plant in Perak, comprising RM8.4 billion in capacity charges and RM16.2 billion in supply charges.
Lim Guan Eng, the Bagan MP and former Penang chief minister, said on November 20 that Chow had ignored written objections from five independent PBAHB directors over the RM210 million PBAPP must pay Perak each year, even if no water or less than the contracted amount is supplied.
Lim said he supports sourcing water from Perak but objects to the financial terms, and claimed the full agreement had not been disclosed because of non-disclosure provisions.
Chow said on November 19 that the capacity charge was an “availability payment” that recovers the plant’s construction cost and is separate from payment for water actually supplied.
He said PBAPP pays the supply charge only for water it receives, and that safeguards in the agreement include compensation for shortfalls, a right to terminate and renegotiation if supply is suspended for more than three months.

Title: Not a specialist yet, so no specialist pay: Health DG explains on-call allowance row
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 21 — Medical officers undergoing Supervised Work Experience (SWE) are only eligible for the On-Call Allowance (Etap) at the medical officer rate until they are officially gazetted as specialists, according to the Ministry of Health (MOH).
Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab, in a statement today, said that payment of the allowance was based on the rates and eligibility criteria applicable to medical officers under the existing service circulars, even if they had completed their specialist training.
However, he said the MOH provides the Pre-Gazettement Specialist Incentive Payment to officers who meet the eligibility requirements, in recognition of their contributions throughout the SWE period.
“Throughout the SWE period, officers carry out clinical responsibilities and on-call duties under supervision. As they have yet to be gazetted as medical specialists, Etap is paid based on the rates and eligibility criteria applicable to medical officers under the existing service circulars,” he said.
The clarification follows public concerns over Etap payments to medical officers undergoing SWE.
Dr Mahathar said SWE is a mandatory period of supervised work experience under a medical specialist after an officer has completed specialist training, before being registered as a specialist in the National Specialist Register (NSR) under the Malaysian Medical Council.
He said the requirement was in line with amendments to the Medical Act 1971 through the Medical (Amendment) Act 2024, particularly subparagraph 14B(1)(d)(i).
“Upon completing SWE and fulfilling all the stipulated specialist recognition requirements, including registration in the NSR and gazettement as a medical specialist through a Specialist Gazette Letter, officers may be considered for the Specialist Etap and Specialist Incentive Payment, subject to the General Orders and the regulations and eligibility requirements in force,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dr Mahathar said the MOH assured that it would continue to review any improvements to the policies and eligibility criteria for allowance payments comprehensively, in consultation with the relevant central agencies.
He said the review would consider officers’ welfare, public service requirements, and compliance with service regulations and financial governance.
The MOH also welcomed public feedback but hoped that any issues concerning implementation would be channelled through official avenues to avoid confusion over public service procedures, he added. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Etap stands for Elaun Tugas Atas Panggilan in Malay.

Title: Real test of China ties is how many Malaysian SMEs join global supply chains, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Kingfa, Plastech China and Eternal Asia are exploring opportunities to source supplies from Malaysia, covering speciality chemicals, polymers and palm-based products.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said foreign investments also open significant opportunities for Malaysian companies to become suppliers to global corporations.
He made the remarks in a post on his social media platform today following his participation in the Malaysia-China High-Level Trade and Investment Dialogue in Shenzhen, alongside Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The dialogue brought together 23 leading Chinese companies, including Tencent, Xiaomi and EVE Energy.
Tengku Zafrul said China recorded RM38.6 billion in approved investments in Malaysia during the first nine months of 2026.
“In my view, the success of these economic ties must also be measured by how many Malaysian small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and suppliers have successfully gained access to international supply chains,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Perak MB lauds MRCB for upgrading rural Lenggong school under Madani Adopted Schools programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad has praised Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) for upgrading a rural school in Lenggong under the Madani Adopted Schools programme, Scoop reported.
Saarani, a former teacher, visited SMK Dato’ Ahmad yesterday, where MRCB had refurbished the teachers’ room and digital room. The upgrade included air-conditioning, wireless connectivity and a podcast studio corner.
“Usually, the teachers’ rooms in rural schools are always the ones left neglected, yet our teachers toil in the sweltering weather to educate our children,” he was quoted as saying.
The Kota Tampan assemblyman said the facilities would be a big motivation for students in rural areas.
Saarani also called for discipline duties to be returned to school disciplinary teachers, given the rising number of bullying cases in public and residential schools, the news portal reported.
According to Scoop, MRCB engineers and officers made trips of more than 100km every week for several months to carry out the work. They had to deal with limited resources and slow internet because of the school’s rural location, but the school has since been fully digitalised.
MRCB executive vice-president Datuk Dell Akbar Khan, a former national footballer, described how MRCB staff went to the school in person to help with the refurbishment.
Saarani also credited MRCB for developing the Ipoh Central rail station, a project worth over RM6 billion. He said the role of corporate entities in helping Perak must not be underestimated.
SMK Dato’ Ahmad teacher Aziah Adam, who retires next month, thanked MRCB for the upgrade.
“For the last 30 years, our teachers’ room only had ceiling and table fans. Now in weeks before I retire, my colleagues and I would be marking examination papers while enjoying cool air.
“It is a fitting farewell gift, that the teaching profession is getting the support it deserves,” she was quoted as saying.
Saarani’s wife, Datin Seri Aezer Zubin, a retired teacher, has a past link to SMK Dato’ Ahmad, which made the visit a personal one for the couple.
The other schools MRCB has adopted under the programme are SMK Kampung Selamat in Tasek Gelugor and SK Pulau Aman in Simpang Ampat, both in Penang, and SK Guar Jentik and SK Felda Mata Air in Kangar, Perlis.

Title: Report: LTAT board picks Achi Jaya as preferred buyer for BPlant, final nod rests with PM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) is expected to meet Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim soon to discuss the proposed sale of Boustead Plantations Bhd (BPlant) to Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd, Sinar Harian reported.
Citing information it had obtained, the Malay daily said LTAT’s board of directors is believed to have already chosen Achi Jaya as its preferred buyer.
However, the deal, which is reportedly worth about RM3.5 billion, still needs the prime minister’s final approval, the daily said.
The report comes after LTAT said in an official statement on Nov 18 that no definitive agreement had been signed. That statement neither confirmed nor denied whether a preferred bidder had been identified.
LTAT said at the time that all bidders were assessed against criteria set earlier. These included company status, financing capability, strategic fit and commitment to the Malaysian Armed Forces community.
Sinar Harian said Achi Jaya is a private plantation company that earlier reports had linked, through its corporate ownership, to the family of the late former Sarawak chief minister Tun Abdul Taib Mahmud.
The daily said the proposed sale has raised concerns among stakeholders, including NGOs representing military veterans. The concerns are about how the buyer was chosen and whether it makes sense to sell the plantation assets when the company’s finances are reportedly improving.
In 2023, Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) proposed buying a 33 per cent stake in BPlant at RM1.55 per share, which valued the company’s total equity at about RM3.47 billion. That proposal was later called off.

Title: Integrity can’t just be preached, it must be practised, says UKM chancellor Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
BANGI, Nov 21 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has called for integrity, transparency and accountability to be put into practice in every aspect of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia’s (UKM) administration to strengthen public confidence in the institution.
His Royal Highness, who is also UKM chancellor, said integrity should not merely be a principle that is proclaimed, but must instead be reflected in the university’s financial management, administration and every decision it makes.
“Transparency, accountability and checks and balances must go hand in hand with efficiency. It is through such practices that public confidence in UKM can be strengthened,” he said at the 54th UKM convocation ceremony here today.
Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, UKM pro-chancellor Tan Sri Datuk Rafiah Salim, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and UKM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh.
Tuanku Muhriz said following the controversy that occurred last year and in the preceding years, the university’s Board of Directors and management had undertaken reforms to strengthen its governance and administration.
His Royal Highness said the initiatives included the establishment of an Ad Hoc Governance Committee and the appointment of independent consultants to conduct a comprehensive assessment of UKM’s governance practices.
“The assessment was conducted over 32 weeks and covered the governance of the UKM Group, finance and procurement. This initiative reflects UKM’s willingness to undergo objective evaluation and implement reforms.
“Indeed, strong governance depends not only on structures and procedures, but also on the values upheld by every member of the UKM community. As stated in the report presented to me, governance standards endure only when they are understood, practised and upheld by the people who lead, manage and serve the university. Therefore, this new initiative is very timely,” Tuanku Muhriz said.
In this regard, Tuanku Muhriz called for a university work culture founded on trustworthiness, integrity, professionalism, courtesy and accountability, while ensuring that talent development and leadership appointments were based on merit and competence.
His Royal Highness also expressed hope that the development of the UKM Code of Conduct and The UKM Way guidelines would strengthen the adoption of these values among members of the university community.
Tuanku Muhriz also expressed appreciation for UKM’s initiatives to establish the Tuanku Muhriz Royal Chair in Integrity and Good Governance, as well as the Centre for Governance and Good Regulatory Practices.
On the convocation, His Royal Highness expressed delight to celebrate more than 14,000 graduates receiving their degrees at this year’s ceremony.
His Royal Highness congratulated national track cycling champion Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang, who was conferred an Honorary Doctor of Philosophy (Sports Development) in recognition of his contributions to the development of sports in the country.
Nine UKM academic figures were also conferred the title of Professor Emeritus in recognition of their scholarly contributions to the university and the nation, while two graduates received the Royal Education Award.
Tuanku Muhriz also reminded graduates that obtaining a degree was not the end of their learning journey, but rather the beginning of a greater responsibility to contribute to society.
His Royal Highness urged graduates to continue upgrading their skills, updating their knowledge and safeguarding the university’s good name as alumni. — Bernama

Title: Tuhau, not tenderloin? Sabah wants a rethink of how poverty is measured
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 21 — Sabah’s Food Poverty Line Income (PGK) calculation method needs to be reviewed to ensure a more accurate measure of poverty that reflects local living conditions, culture and dietary habits, particularly in rural areas, said Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) Secretariat chief coordinating officer Datuk Datu Rosmadi Datu Sulai.
He said the measurement method should take into account the unique characteristics of Sabah’s communities, whose dietary needs and practices differ from those in Peninsular Malaysia.
He said Sabah’s PGK was currently almost on par with that of Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, but the food items used in the calculation did not necessarily reflect the consumption patterns of the state’s population.
“On the ground in Sabah, when I look at the list of food items that Sabahans are required to buy or choose from, it is the same as that used in Peninsular Malaysia, particularly Kuala Lumpur and Selangor,” he told Bernama.
Rosmadi said examples of this mismatch included meat consumption among non-Muslim communities in Sabah, as well as seafood such as crabs, prawns and shellfish, which formed part of the staple diet of coastal communities.
Local vegetables such as tuhau (wild ginger) and lembiding (a type of fern), which were not included in the food components used as references, were other examples.
He said these differences could affect the calculation of food costs and, consequently, the determination of the number of people living in poverty.
He cited an example in which more than 55,000 people classified as living in absolute poverty in Sabah could instead fall into the B40 income group if Perlis’ food poverty line income were used as the benchmark.
Rosmadi said the state government, through the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) 2.0 Development Plan, aimed to reduce Sabah’s poverty rate from 17.7 per cent in 2024 to between three and five per cent by 2030, focusing on five priorities: housing, education, employment, welfare, as well as entrepreneurship and training.
Meanwhile, Sabah Department of Statistics Malaysia director Khairolnizam Hassan said the department took note of Rosmadi’s views, particularly the types of staple foods consumed by local communities, and would examine the proposal to improve the calculation method.
He explained that the PGK was calculated based on calorie requirements set in accordance with Health Ministry guidelines and the spending patterns of the lowest-income households, while differences in food prices and household sizes between states also influenced their respective poverty line income figures.
He said Sabah’s food PGK was influenced by higher food prices compared with several other states, as well as Sabah’s average household size of between 4.5 and five people, which increased a family’s food expenditure requirements.
He said that based on the 2024 absolute poverty statistics, nine of the 10 districts with the highest poverty rates in Malaysia were in Sabah, namely Pitas, Tongod, Kota Marudu, Kudat, Beluran, Membakut, Kinabatangan, Kalabakan and Kota Belud, while the remaining district was Daro in Sarawak.
He said the poverty classification was based on the PGK set for each state, with Sabah’s overall PGK standing at RM2,873 per month.
Households earning below this threshold were classified as poor.
Meanwhile, Kinabatangan Member of Parliament Datuk Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar also supported the proposal to review Sabah’s poverty measurement method by taking into account geographical factors, logistics costs and difficulties in accessing necessities and services, particularly in rural areas.
He said the Market Basket Measure approach used in Canada could serve as a reference, as it accounted for differences in logistics costs and the prices of goods in remote areas when setting the poverty line.
“The Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation approach in Scotland should also be studied as it takes into account various socioeconomic factors and geographical considerations, including the time taken by residents to travel to access facilities and services,” he said.
Naim said this was particularly important given the vast size of the Kinabatangan constituency and the considerable distances between villages, which posed unique challenges for residents.
He said it was regrettable that Kinabatangan and Tongod, two districts within his constituency, were among the poorest districts in Malaysia and the situation required immediate action.
He said efforts to increase residents’ incomes should be prioritised through the development of the agriculture sector and downstream industries, including timber processing, while making use of the Kinabatangan strategic development plan drawn up in collaboration with the Institute for Development Studies (Sabah) and Universiti Malaysia Sabah. — Bernama

Title: Perak school squeeze to ease with 844-seat SK Seri Chemor in 2032
Article:
IPOH, Nov 21 — The planned construction of Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Seri Chemor near here has brought relief to local residents grappling with student overcrowding at primary schools around Chemor and Chepor.
For civil servant Kamalul Hayyat Abdul Rani, 33, who lives at Dataran Kinding SSI, Tanjung Rambutan, the proposed new school is welcome news for parents because limited capacity at existing schools often complicates registration for their children.
The father of two boys aged seven and three said the new school would ease his family’s daily routine because it is close to his mother-in-law’s house in Tanah Hitam, where his children stay before and after school.
“Schools are already crowded now. If you register late, for instance, it becomes a problem when intake is full,” he told Bernama recently.
Kamalul Hayyat also intends to enrol his youngest son at SK Seri Chemor, noting the journey from his mother-in-law’s house to the school takes five minutes.
Echoing the sentiment, private-sector procurement executive Mohammad Hasiff Radzi, 34, described the construction of SK Seri Chemor as a timely move amid the rapid growth of housing estates and population around Chemor.
The Taman Chemor Idaman resident, father of three children aged seven, five and nine months, said the school’s location, five minutes’ drive from his home, would add convenience for nearby families.
“Whether it is opening a primary school or a secondary school, any addition is welcome because the local population is growing rapidly,” he said.
He expressed confidence that the school’s comprehensive facilities, including mainstream classes, preschool and the Integrated Special Education Programme (PPKI), would make it a top choice for local parents, including himself, when enrolling children.
Perak Education director Datuk Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar said the construction of SK Seri Chemor, approved under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) Rolling Plan 1 (RP1) with an allocation of RM80 million, was planned to ease overcrowding pressure in the area.
He said two nearby primary schools, SK Haji Mahmud and SK Chepor, currently operate in two sessions due to high enrolments of 1,043 and 1,041 pupils, respectively.
The new site on Lot 153789, owned by the Federal Lands Commissioner (PTP) in the Tambun parliamentary constituency, is on the same lot as Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Dato’ Haji Mohd Taib.
“So with the establishment of SK Seri Chemor, it is expected to meet the needs of local residents. Indirectly, we can also decongest existing overcrowded schools,” he told Bernama in an interview at his office here recently.
Commenting on the school’s development plan, Zulkafli said SK Seri Chemor is designed to accommodate a total capacity of 844 pupils across 34 classrooms.
According to him, the breakdown includes 24 mainstream classrooms for 720 pupils, six PPKI classrooms for 42 pupils, three mainstream preschool classrooms for 75 pupils and one integrated preschool (PPKI) classroom for seven pupils.
Zulkafli said the school will also be equipped with various physical facilities and special rooms meeting required standards, including a field and a canteen, to create a more comfortable and conducive learning environment for all pupils.
He stressed that the new school building’s design prioritised the welfare and comfort of pupils with special needs, ensuring no group of students is marginalised.
Based on current planning, SK Seri Chemor is expected to be completed in 2031 and begin operations in 2032, subject to smooth execution of design, construction and project handover phases through close cooperation between the state government, the Federal Government, contractors and appointed consultants, he added.
During the tabling of Budget 2027, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the government would build several new schools, preschool buildings and facilities at existing schools, including SK Seri Chemor in Ipoh. — Bernama

Title: Two young children killed as fire destroys 90pc of house in Kedah village
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Two children, aged one year and four months and three years old, were found burnt on a bed after a fire broke out at a house in Kampung Teloi Tua, Sik, Kedah early this morning.
Sinar Harian reported that firefighters from the Sik Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene at 6.27am, shortly after receiving an emergency call.
The Fire and Rescue Department said in a statement that the fire involved a house measuring 20 by 10 feet, and that about 90 per cent of it was destroyed.
“The firefighting operation used two hose streams, with water sourced from the fire engine’s tank and a fire hydrant.
“Two victims were found on the bed and confirmed dead,” it said in the statement, as quoted by the Malay daily.
A nearby volunteer fire team, the police and the Health Ministry also assisted in the operation.
Sinar Harian reported that firefighters were still putting out the remaining fire and carrying out overhaul work at the scene, and that investigations into the incident are ongoing.

Title: Trailer runs red light, hits and drags teen motorcyclist at Kampar junction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — A 19-year-old college student survived after a trailer hit his motorcycle and dragged it at a traffic light junction near a supermarket in Kampar, Perak yesterday.
Sinar Harian reported that the accident happened at about 3.45pm at Kilometre 34 of Jalan Ipoh-Kuala Lumpur. It went viral after dashcam footage of the crash was shared on social media.
The footage shows a trailer ploughing into the motorcycle as it crossed the junction, knocking the rider down and dragging him along the road. Members of the public who stopped to help were seen calming the victim.
Kampar district police chief Superintendent Mohamad Nazri Daud told the Malay daily that the victim survived with injuries to his left leg.
He said the trailer, driven by a 48-year-old man, was believed to have run a red light while travelling from Kampar towards Ipoh.
“The trailer then collided with the Honda motorcycle ridden by the victim, who was coming from the left.
“As a result of the collision, the victim, a college student, suffered serious injuries to his leg, while the trailer driver sustained head injuries,” he was quoted as saying.
Mohamad Nazri said the trailer driver had been detained to assist investigations under Section 43 of the Road Transport Act 1987. A urine test on him came back negative.
“Further investigations are under way to determine the actual cause of the accident and to complete the investigation papers,” he said.

Title: Kota Kinabalu stabbing: Sabah police nab suspected killer at Tawau jetty after six-day manhunt
Article:
TAWAU, Nov 21 — Police arrested a 38-year-old man sought in connection with a fatal stabbing in Kuala Manggatal, Kota Kinabalu, at the Tawau Public Jetty around 11.30am on Friday.
District police chief ACP Rosdi Mat Jusoh confirmed that the suspect, who had been wanted since Nov 15, was detained to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
An inspection of the suspect led to the discovery of a branded smartphone and a waist pouch believed to be linked to the case.
Rosdi urged the public not to speculate or spread unverified information that could compromise ongoing police investigations.
Kota Kinabalu police had previously circulated the local man's photograph and identity to the media on November 15 to assist in investigating the fatal stabbing of a 31-year-old man at Sulaman Central. — Daily Express
* Editor’s note: ACP stands for Assistant Commissioner of Police.

Title: Pay RM900m before December sitting of state legislative assembly, Sabah Pakatan tells Putrajaya
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 21 — Sabah (PH) Pakatan Harapan wants the federal government to disburse the remaining RM900 million in interim payments for Sabah’s 40 per cent revenue entitlement before the State Legislative Assembly sitting next month.
Sabah PH chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the interim payment had been increased to RM1.5 billion, comprising RM600 million that had already been gazetted and paid, while the remaining RM900 million was being processed.
“We want the payment to be made before the State Legislative Assembly sitting this December.
“I have personally met Tan Sri Johan Merican, the secretary-general of the Treasury, to convey the state government’s request for the payment to be released.
“We also want the amount to be fully disbursed so that it can be incorporated into the state’s revenue for next year and used for expenditure on matters concerning the interests and welfare of the people,” he told a press conference here yesterday.
Mustapha said Sabah PH was also proposing that future interim payments be increased progressively each year, rather than remain at a fixed amount for five years.
“At present, when an amount is gazetted, its value remains unchanged for five years.
“We propose that, starting next year, the gazetted amount should increase progressively each year, based on the revenue generated by federal government agencies in Sabah.
“We do not want the RM1.5 billion to remain fixed for five years. We want a progressive arrangement.
“The amount to be returned to the state government should be negotiated with the federal government and mutually agreed upon. This is our proposal until we achieve the actual 40 per cent entitlement,” he said.
He said both the federal and state governments should agree on a progressive payment mechanism to ensure that Sabah’s 40 per cent revenue entitlement would eventually be realised.
Mustapha explained that discussions on the interim payments were being conducted through technical and main committees involving representatives from Sabah and Sarawak.
The technical committee is chaired by Deputy Prime Minister II Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, with Mustapha serving as deputy chairman.
Representatives from both states, including their respective deputy chief ministers, are also involved in the discussions. — The Borneo Post
